Its mean peak GPU memory usage is $91.0\%$--$93.3\%$ lower than that of the same baselines. Experiments with different sensor configurations validate the adaptability of the shared acquisition pipeline, while flights in nine real-world scenes further demonstrate onboard closed-loop operation under practical computational and motion constraints.

papers.title: Sharp minimax rates and adaptive estimation of latent proportions in bivariate Poisson mixtures
papers.abstract: We study estimation of the mean latent composition in a bivariate Poisson mixture. Conditional on an unobserved intensity S and proportion U, two counts are independent Poisson variables with respective means SU and S(1-U). The mixing law is unrestricted on the Cartesian product [a,b] x [0,1], where a and b are finite constants satisfying 0 < a < b, and dependence between S and U is allowed. Although the mixing distribution is identifiable, the usual ratio of mean counts estimates an intensity-weighted proportion and may be biased for theta = E[U]. We construct polynomial estimators based on factorial moments and establish the exact leading exponent of the minimax squared-error risk on the logarithmic scale, without claiming an exact multiplicative minimax constant. We also derive the sharp logarithmic separation exponent for testing zero latent covariance and construct an adaptive estimator achieving parametric squared-error risk on the zero-covariance submodel while retaining the optimal full-model logarithmic minimax exponent. Simulations illustrate the bias-variance trade-off, the role of polynomial regularization, and the distinction between theoretically guaranteed and empirically calibrated adaptation.

papers.title: Agentic Scaling of Embodied Tasks in Simulation for Synthetic Data Collection and Policy Evaluation
papers.abstract: Scaling embodied interaction data requires a broad collection of usable tasks, yet specifying and validating each task instance remains costly. We present AgenticTask, an agent-based framework that expands existing task collections under human intent. Its central representation links interaction requirements to object and part bindings, scene and robot configurations, initial conditions, and completion criteria. A task-generation agent reuses interaction structure to construct supported variations and revises incompatible configurations using validation feedback. A task-execution agent uses the same bindings and geometric records to select robot-supported skills and check completion against the original task criteria. On RoboCasa, the framework builds the AgenticTask collection, saving 16,450 task instances from 20,323 construction attempts at a throughput of 166.97 saved instances per elapsed hour, with 62.26% of construction attempts passing the configured physical checks. The execution agent completes approximately 38% of evaluated tasks, with successful cases spanning object placement, articulated manipulation, and sequential arrangement. Diagnostic analysis identifies improvement priorities in construction reliability, action selection, task-robot compatibility, and runtime integration. Together, these results demonstrate task-collection expansion with measured construction productivity and concrete execution evidence, providing a foundation for subsequent interaction-data collection for embodied AI.

papers.title: PaveSplat: Resolution-Robust Feed-Forward Gaussian Splatting with Residually Corrected Surface-Aligned Covariances
papers.abstract: We present PaveSplat, a feed-forward Gaussian splatting method that adds a learned residual to the analytic surface-aligned covariance, keeping surfels paving the visible surface across rendering resolutions. Pixel-aligned feed-forward Gaussian splatting predicts one primitive per pixel from a few images in a single pass, and its rendering quality depends on how well these primitives cover the surface. Recent surfel-based methods compute the surface-aligned covariance analytically from predicted depth. However, this covariance has no way to correct the surfel orientation where the depth-derived frame is ill-posed. The surfels then cover the surface loosely; at the training resolution each surfel's one-pixel minimum footprint covers the gaps, but they show up as holes when the same prediction is re-rendered at a higher resolution. To address this, we keep the analytic covariance as an initialization, with its axes aligned to the surface tangents, and add an identity-initialized unit-quaternion residual that reorients a surfel only where this improves rendering, turning surfels that the analytic frame mis-aims back onto the surface. On RealEstate10K, PaveSplat achieves the best PSNR, SSIM, and LPIPS among single-Gaussian-per-pixel methods at every scale (1x-8x). The native-resolution gain is small; the benefit appears when the same prediction is rendered at higher display resolutions without re-running the network. On zero-shot DL3DV, it leads PSNR within this group at every scale and ranks first or second on SSIM/LPIPS. A coverage-hole analysis shows fewer uncovered pixels than both baselines under high-resolution re-rendering.

papers.title: Variational Trajectory Flow Matching with a Non-Linear Interpolant
papers.abstract: Simulation-free methods such as Trajectory Flow Matching learn dynamics by regressing the time derivative of a local interpolant placed between consecutive observations. The interpolant defines the regression target, and under sparse, irregular sampling, it underrepresents the dynamics and bounds what can be learned. We show that no fixed interpolant dominates: the best of linear, quadratic, spline and quintic changes with the system and with the sampling density. We propose to learn the interpolant instead. An amortized implicit neural representation (INR) is fitted to the training trajectories and frozen as a teacher supplying the target velocity to a learnable velocity field. We further frame the velocity field within a variational framework, yielding a probabilistic forecaster that, at inference, requires only the velocity field and no SDE solver. We evaluate our method on a range of dynamical systems: it consistently achieves high accuracy and more stable long-horizon rollouts under sparser observations, at matched velocity-field capacity.

papers.title: Strong Field Tidal Disruptions of Rotating Stars by Spinning Black Holes
papers.abstract: We study tidal disruptions of rotating solar-type stars by a rapidly spinning supermassive black hole with general-relativistic smoothed-particle hydrodynamics. To capture strong-field effects, we place the pericentre at a few gravitational radii of a black hole, and compare with weak-field encounters at a larger pericentre around a lighter black hole. We vary the black hole spin, the orbital inclination and the stellar rotation, using rigidly and differentially rotating stars with spin aligned, anti-aligned or perpendicular to the orbital angular momentum. In the strong field, the black hole spin decides whether a core survives on equatorial and inclined orbits, and stellar rotation reduces the surviving core in every partial disruption. At the larger pericentre, as in Newtonian studies, anti-aligned rotation instead protects the star from disruption. In both cases the tide reverses an anti-aligned spin just before pericentre. The outcome differs because in the strong field the tide keeps acting on the reversed core long after pericentre. Deep encounters leave cores spinning above break-up, which shed mass and angular momentum as they settle. Full disruptions approach the canonical fallback law, whereas the late-time slope of partial disruptions is not universal and is set by the debris energy distribution near the surviving core.

papers.title: Bifurcation analysis of particulate Rayleigh-Benard convection
papers.abstract: Particles carried through a convecting fluid layer exchange momentum and heat with the fluid, and so change not only where convection starts but also how it saturates. We study this coupling in the particulate Rayleigh-Benard system, in which a dilute stream of thermally inertial particles is injected at one wall and removed at the other. An Eulerian two-fluid model retaining drag, pressure-gradient, added-mass, and buoyancy forces and interphase heat exchange describes heavy particles and bubbles through a single density parameter beta. After reproducing the linear stability results of Raza et al. (2025a), we use a multiple-scale expansion and a Fredholm solvability condition to compute the first Landau coefficient a1 near onset. At low and moderate particle loading, the bifurcation is supercritical for every density ratio considered, extending the conclusion of Srinivas and Tomar (2025) for very heavy particles. At higher flux, however, Re(a1) changes sign, and the onset becomes subcritical over a broad band of density ratios, from moderately heavy particles injected below their terminal speed to most light particles. In the plane of density ratio and injection velocity, this band is bounded by lines of tricritical points. Splitting a1 by the balance equation shows that its sign is set almost entirely by the fluid energy equation, while the direct nonlinear terms of the particle equations are five to six orders of magnitude smaller. The particles thus change the nature of the bifurcation indirectly, through the base state and the linear mode they help to shape, rather than through their own nonlinear dynamics.

papers.title: Optimal Beurling-Hörmander-type uncertainty principles and nontriviality of Gelfand-Shilov spaces
papers.abstract: We study how rapidly a nonzero function $f \in L^2(\mathbb{R})$ and its Fourier transform $\widehat{f}$ can simultaneously decay. For each suitable weight function $ω$, we construct a convex weight function $\varpi$ and establish the existence of a threshold $Φ_{(ω,\varpi^*)} \in (0, \infty)$, where $\varpi^*$ denotes the convex conjugate of $\varpi$. For $a,b > 0$, the conditions \[ \int_{-\infty}^\infty |f(x)| e^{ω(a|x|)} \, \mathrm{d}x < \infty \qquad \text{and} \qquad \int_{-\infty}^\infty |\widehat{f}(ξ)| e^{\varpi^*(b|ξ|)} \, \mathrm{d}ξ < \infty \] force $f = 0$ when $ab > Φ_{(ω,\varpi^*)}$, whereas the functions satisfying both conditions form a dense subspace of $L^2(\mathbb{R})$ when $ab < Φ_{(ω,\varpi^*)}$. Similar results are also established in higher dimensions. We characterize the weights $ω$ for which $\varpi$ is equivalent to $ω$ and use this to determine when the Beurling-Hörmander uncertainty principle is optimal. A discrete form of the same construction yields a characterization of the nontriviality of Gelfand-Shilov spaces $\mathcal{S}^{M}_{A}(\mathbb{R}^d)$ and $Σ^{M}_{A}(\mathbb{R}^d)$ in terms of their defining weight sequences $M$ and $A$, under suitable regularity assumptions.

papers.title: Streaming-AAA: Streaming AAA Game Video Generation at High Resolution, High Frame Rate, and Low Latency
papers.abstract: Controllable streaming video generation offers a promising route toward interactive game simulation, yet existing methods remain far from practical gameplay. They often fail to jointly achieve high visual fidelity, high frame rates, and low interaction latency, resulting in poor responsiveness and degraded user experience. We present Streaming-AAA, a new paradigm for controllable infinite generation of AAA-quality game videos. Our system generates 1080p gameplay videos at 43 FPS with 198 ms end-to-end latency interaction on merely NVIDIA A800 GPUs, while supporting long-horizon play without severe temporal degradation or collapse. Streaming-AAA is built upon three key designs. First, we redesign the VAE architecture for efficient high-resolution decoding, enabling real-time synthesis at 1080p. Second, we pretrain the diffusion model using diffusion forcing and significantly extend the temporal training horizon, allowing the model to capture long-term dependencies and maintain persistent memory. Third, we perform post-training distillation and memory compression to improve inference efficiency while retaining visual quality and temporal consistency. Experiments show that Streaming-AAA substantially improves visual fidelity, frame rate, latency, and long-term stability over prior controllable video generation approaches, enabling a significantly more playable experience for interactive AAA game video generation.

papers.title: Three-mode chimera-like states in a minimal network of active camphor ribbons
papers.abstract: Chimera states are a remarkable manifestation of symmetry breaking, wherein identical units spontaneously split into coherent and incoherent groups. The term "chimera" itself is inspired by the mythological creature having parts of different animals, reflecting the coexistence of distinct dynamical behaviors within a single system. Here, we experimentally demonstrate the existence of a three-mode chimera-like state in a system of four identical camphor-infused elliptical rotors, each pivoted at a corner of a square base. When placed on a water surface, the rotors self-propel and rotate due to Marangoni-driven flows. Chemical coupling mediated through the shared water interface gives rise to three distinct collective dynamical states, namely a synchronized one, an antisynchronized one and an incoherent one. Our results validate recent theoretical work about three-domain chimeras in reaction-diffusion models, providing new insights into nonlinear dynamics and suggesting that this new type of chimera may be observed in a broad class of physical systems.

papers.title: Channel-Aware Codebook Design for Task-Oriented Token Communication Over Wireless Networks
papers.abstract: This paper investigates the adaptive codebook design for task-oriented token communication over wireless networks with dynamic channels. This paper proposes the channel-aware codebook (CAC), a joint channel- and reconstruction-driven framework that reorders the labels of a frozen 14-bit VQGAN codebook. In the considered framework, a balanced geometric partition forms prefix groups, a prefix bijection places the groups on the label hypercube, and bijective suffix assignments place the codewords within each group. The problem is formulated to minimize the expected full-image perceptual distortion of the frozen decoder under a binary symmetric channel, averaged over a design set of bit error rates (BERs) and retaining simultaneous token errors. An offline algorithm alternates prefix and suffix exchanges and screens and confirms candidates on paired batches under a fixed decoder-evaluation budget. The assignment preserves the error-free reconstruction and the payload and deploys as static lookup tables without retraining. Under the binary symmetric channel at BER $0.01$, it reduces LPIPS by $12.3\%$ and improves COCO AP by $14.1\%$ ($1.72$ points) relative to the native labels, and it lowers LPIPS by a further $4.5\%$ relative to a related assignment adaptation at the same payload.

papers.title: An improved Moore bound for girths seven and eleven
papers.abstract: Let $n(d,k)$ be the minimum number of vertices of a graph of minimum degree $d$ and girth at least $g=2k+1$. A simple counting argument gives the classical lower bound $n(d,k)\ge m(d,k)=1+d\sum_{i=0}^{k-1}(d-1)^i$, known as the Moore bound and dating back at least to 1960. Apart from complete graphs and odd cycles, graphs attaining this lower bound can exist only for girth $5$ and degrees $3,7$ and $57$ (Hoffman and Singleton 1960; Bannai and Ito 1973; Damerell 1973). Nevertheless, for more than sixty years this lower bound has not been substantially improved beyond an additive constant. For $k\geq 3$, i.e. girth at least $7$, the best general bound was $n(d,k)\ge m(d,k)+2$, due to Bannai and Ito (1981). We show that for fixed girth $7$ and growing degree $d$ we have $n(d,3)\ge m(d,3)+(1-o(1))d/8$. Furthermore, for girth $11$ we have $n(d,5)\ge m(d,5)+Ω(d^{3/5})$. In particular, the excess $n(d,k)-m(d,k)$, for $k\in\{3,5\}$, tends to infinity with $d$ and is therefore generally unbounded, which answers a question of Bollobás from 1978. For the degree/diameter problem we obtain similar bounds. A graph of maximum degree $d$ and diameter $3$ or $5$ has at most $m(d,3)-Ω(\sqrt{d})$ or $m(d,5)-Ω(d^{3/10})$ vertices, respectively. This answers a question of Bermond and Bollobás from 1981: for every constant $c$ there are $d$ and $k$ such that every graph of maximum degree $d$ and diameter $k$ has at least $c$ fewer vertices than the Moore bound.

papers.title: Presenting Your Figures: Data-informed Animated Transitions Across Scientific Figure Panels
papers.abstract: Multi-panel figures are commonly used in research papers to show scientific data, and researchers often reuse them when presenting their work. Presenting these figures often involves explaining how data across chart panels are related. Animated transitions can progressively reveal these relationships, but two static panels specify only the endpoints, leaving what intermediate keyframes should show and how the transition should progress unclear. To support transition design across diverse scientific figures, we developed Figure Space and Transition Space through iterative analysis of 48 published multi-panel figures across eight scientific subject areas. Figure Space represents panel composition, data transformations, and visual encodings while retaining the links needed to trace panel results back to records. Transition Space uses this representation and source data to construct and sequence keyframes that make corresponding data visible and align them while preserving the meaning of each panel's position encodings. Building on these spaces, we developed FigFlux, a human-in-the-loop authoring system that guides AI agents in generating animated transitions from a multi-panel figure and its associated materials. Researchers can revise keyframes in natural language before animation generation. We evaluate FigFlux through cross-domain case studies, a study with 16 scientific authors, and expert assessment. Authors reported lower overall workload than with their familiar tools, while experts gave FigFlux transitions higher ratings than transitions created with participants' familiar tools or generated by AI alone. The example gallery have been published online: https://figflux.github.io.

papers.title: Fixing the Twin, Not the Detector: Sim-to-Real Roadside LiDAR Detection from Digital-Twin Data
papers.abstract: Roadside LiDAR detectors are expensive to train on real labels, and digital twins promise to replace these labels, but a detector trained on a twin meets a different sensor, different objects and different annotation conventions on the real site. We describe the pipeline that placed first in the LUMPI track of the UrbanTwin Sim2Real LiDAR Challenge (IEEE BigData 2026 Cup, 0.5541 combined score) and fifth on its V2X-Real track (0.8102). Every detector is a CenterPoint model trained only on synthetic data, on a single 8 GB laptop GPU. Most of the gain came from correcting differences between the twin and the real site rather than from the detector. We align the twin's coordinates, point density and box convention with the test sensor, generate the pedestrians and riders that the twins lack, plus street clutter as unlabeled negatives, and rebuild twin objects at real size and real point density. A non-learned resampling to the per-cell point density of unlabeled real frames lifts LUMPI realism from 0.589 to 0.947, against 0.949 between real frames. Label-free post-processing then exploits what a fixed roadside sensor guarantees: static structures recur in every frame, and real objects have characteristic point statistics. Reporting the validation and test gain of each component side by side, we find that corrections of systematic sim-to-real differences transfer to the test set, typically keeping a quarter to three quarters of their validation gain, while choices that fit the few objects of a validation set do not.

papers.title: Stars and paths in oriented graphs
papers.abstract: Let $\overrightarrow{F}$ be a fixed oriented graph. Its oriented Turán number, written $\exo(n,\overrightarrow{F})$, is the largest size of an $n$-vertex oriented graph with no copy of $\overrightarrow{F}$. This parameter extends the classical notion of Turán number to oriented graphs. In this paper, we investigate the supersaturation results for the directed path $P_k~(k\geq 2)$ and all oriented stars $\overrightarrow{S}_{p,q}~(0\leq p\leq q$), and all oriented paths of order at most four.

papers.title: SEOYUN: Refusal-Inducing Exam Documents for AI-Glasses Pipelines
papers.abstract: Camera-equipped glasses can convert an examination page into a query to a vision-language model (VLM). Device detection addresses possession; a complementary question is whether an examination document can reduce the usefulness of an unauthorized capture. We present SEOYUN, an application-specific framework for refusal-inducing exam documents, with optical and encoder-level interventions as extensions. We use reverse jailbreaking to describe the direction of the objective: inducing abstention rather than bypassing refusal. Refusal induction and defensive visual prompt injection already have precedents; our contribution is a threat model, analytical limits, and an evaluation protocol for examination use. We distinguish refusal from correct-answer leakage, show why removing an added dummy option is not itself a reduction in the original answer space, and derive a sampling comparison under explicitly stated camera assumptions. The protocol separates digital, simulated, and physical inputs and requires held-out evaluation after subject-specific selection. A local CSAT candidate corpus and rendering harness have been prepared, but this version reports no model-performance measurements, physical validation, or human-subject results. Accordingly, SEOYUN is a research framework, not a validated defense or a basis for allegations against individuals.

papers.title: Dephasing-free plasma acceleration with millijoule picosecond lasers
papers.abstract: Laser-plasma accelerators reach gradients a thousand times above radio-frequency cavities, but need joule-class femtosecond lasers firing about once per second, and electrons outrun the wave. A comb of laser lines spaced by the plasma frequency, each in its own mode of a matched channel, drives a wake moving at the speed of light. In particle-in-cell simulations a 175\,mJ, 0.5\,ps drive holds 21\,GV/m over 10\,mm with a 0.15\,rad phase drift; a test electron gains 208\,MeV, 2.6 times more than in one mode. Because the wave builds up resonantly, the required energy falls steeply with density: a 29\,mJ drive sustains 20\,GV/m, and a 10\,mJ drive, within reach of kilohertz industrial lasers, gives a test electron 170\,MeV over 30\,mm. A simulated stage transfers 5\,\% of the laser energy to the wake; the Manley--Rowe limit is about 18\,\% for five lines.

papers.title: Close&Safe: Maximal Task Preservation for Redundant Manipulators via C-Space Boundary Detour
papers.abstract: Contact-rich manipulation such as wiping, polishing and surface inspection specifies the task as a continuous end-effector trajectory rather than a goal pose. When an obstacle absent from the planning model intersects it, conventional planners return a collision-free path that may differ from the nominal throughout, discarding trajectory that was never obstructed. We present Close&Safe (Close to the intended task, Safe from obstacles), which decouples tracking from avoidance: the nominal is followed exactly wherever it remains feasible, and avoidance acts only on the interval where it is not, so tracking is hindered as little as the obstacle allows. On that interval we sample the configuration-space obstacle boundary within a corridor around the nominal, connect the samples into a roadmap, and search it for the detour that deviates least before rejoining the nominal at the earliest feasible configuration. We evaluate across diverse simulated obstacle configurations, physical Franka experiments, and ablations of key algorithmic components. The results demonstrate collision-free trajectory repair with localized task modification, while recovering 52.4-78% in simulation and on hardware.

papers.title: The Delayed Societal Cost of Unfairness
papers.abstract: Fair machine learning typically evaluates the societal costs of a decision policy -- the loss incurred by the decision-maker (DM) and the unfair distribution of costs among demographic groups of decision-subjects (DS) -- on static data, where reducing one often comes at the expense of the other. Yet decisions change the populations on which they act, and prior work has shown that fairness interventions designed on static data may fail to benefit, or even harm, the disadvantaged group over time. We investigate a complementary question: When can a policy that is Pareto-optimal on pre-deployment data be outperformed by a fairer policy once each is evaluated on the population it induces, reducing costs for one stakeholder without increasing them for the other? In a setting where qualification scores evolve in response to binary decisions and their outcomes, we show that under Rawlsian fairness, which never lowers any group's acceptance rate, placing sufficiently high weight on fairness reduces societal costs whenever accepting disadvantaged DS at the DM's break-even point leaves them in a state less costly to the DM than rejecting them. Under egalitarian fairness, which may lower the advantaged group's acceptance rate, this additionally requires the reduction in DM loss on the disadvantaged group to outweigh the increase on the advantaged group. Under both fairness notions, however, when DM loss is accuracy-based, improvements in the post-deployment population may arise from declining DS qualification, revealing that gains for the DM do not necessarily translate into better outcomes for DS. Our results show that policy-induced population dynamics can overturn apparent performance-fairness trade-offs, allowing fairer policies to reduce the delayed societal costs of decision-making.

papers.title: Serialization Tax in Shared-Latent Exchangeable Decisions
papers.abstract: Accurate item probabilities can produce inaccurate group-level decisions. A system may score each item separately, yet act on whether enough hidden items succeed: show a slate, defer a panel decision, or inspect a batch. When items share an uncertain latent state, independent marginalization preserves means but removes dependence from the aggregate posterior. We call this error the serialization tax. For binary items sharing one success rate, classical convex-order comparisons give a more dispersed exact count law than any independent completion with the same total mean. We quantify variance and total-variation gaps, derive threshold separation under margin conditions, and connect posterior approximation to decision regret. Separate results cover non-binary outcomes, heterogeneous items, and sufficient posterior resolution. TaxScore identifies large hidden blocks with unresolved uncertainty near a decision boundary for routing to richer posterior heads. On pre-specified, hidden-target-free MovieLens 1M/10M audits, existing shared-latent heads improve high-score negative log-likelihood (NLL)/utility from 0.673/0.696 to 0.629/0.723 and from 0.670/0.691 to 0.639/0.715. Routing gives 0.006--0.012 full-population utility gains, with matched controls identifying their sources. Our code is available at https://github.com/SiminChang/Serialization-Tax-in-Shared-Latent-Exchangeable-Decisions.

papers.title: On the dimension of $V$-variable fractals
papers.abstract: Random recursive sets have been used to model a wide range of fractal phenomena, but they can be slow and difficult to generate. $V$-variability address this problem by allowing these sets at most $V$ distinct shapes at each level of magnification. The formulae for the almost sure Hausdorff dimension of both classes is known, and it has been conjectured that (under mild assumptions) the $V$-variable dimension converges to the random recursive dimension as $V\to\infty$. We prove this conjecture.

papers.title: On the contact of regular surfaces in $\mathbb{R}^4$ with toroidal cylinders and their apparent contours
papers.abstract: We study the contact of regular surfaces in $\mathbb{R}^4$ with toroidal cylinders $S^1(r) \times \mathbb{R}^2$. We relate the contact type to the singularities of the corresponding parallel projections along the direction of the axes of the toroidal cylinders, the geometry of the apparent contours under these projections, and the geometry of the original surfaces.

papers.title: Concerning Factorization at Lepton Colliders
papers.abstract: We uncover super-leading logarithms in non-global observables at lepton colliders. They arise from Glauber interactions involving colored partons produced by electromagnetic splittings of the incoming leptons. A three-loop analysis establishes the resulting factorization breaking, which we reconcile with the use of lepton PDFs below the soft veto scale. We conjecture that soft--collinear factorization fails for exclusive observables even in pure QED by identifying a genuine Glauber region in massless QED. This reveals a far richer infrared structure than naively expected.

papers.title: The Ionospheric Cut-off as a Potential Radio Technosignature
papers.abstract: Radio emission generated on a planetary surface must cross the planet's ionosphere before escaping into space: below the local plasma frequency it is reflected back towards the surface. We investigate this process for broadband radio technosignatures (BRaTs) using a Chapman-layer description of photoionised atmospheres. The plasma frequency depends only weakly on stellar XUV irradiation, scaling as $Q_{\infty}^{1/4}$, implying turnover frequencies of 5-40 MHz for most terrestrial habitable-zone planets, potentially rising towards 100 MHz in extreme environments. The basic signature is simple: the continuum of a surface-origin BRaT should be strongly suppressed below a characteristic frequency that can be estimated from the XUV output of the host star, at every orbital phase and for any viewing geometry. Oblique propagation, magnetic fields, and collisional absorption broaden the cut-off into a smooth escape function, $f_{\mathrm{esc}}(ν,φ)$, where $φ$ is the orbital phase. Because the day-night ionisation pattern is anchored to the substellar point rather than to the rotating surface, disc integration adds a second, more discriminating signature: the half-escape frequency $ν_{1/2}$ varies predictably (by about 40-50 per cent over the orbit, depending on the angular emission pattern of the leakage) and remains locked to the orbital ephemeris. Finite atmospheric response times introduce modest phase lags but preserve the modulation. A low-frequency turnover alone is not unique to technology, but one that varies periodically with the orbital period would be difficult to reproduce through known astrophysical processes. Although observationally challenging, the ionospheric cut-off is a potential technosignature diagnostic and a novel probe of exoplanet ionospheres.

papers.title: ForeSeek: Foresight-Driven Reasoning for Long-Form Video Understanding
papers.abstract: Long-form video understanding, as a fundamental yet crucial vision task, is being revolutionized by multimodal large language model (MLLM)-based video agents. However, the retrieval-driven nature inherent to these agents creates a significant bottleneck, forcing them to reactively fetch clips based on local saliency without a global temporal plan. To address this, we present ForeSeek, a foresight-driven video agent that transforms long-video reasoning from reactive retrieval into predictive exploration. Rather than blindly probing the timeline, ForeSeek forms visually grounded expectations over unseen temporal regions, verifies them through targeted observations, and continuously refines its search based on emerging evidence, where failed expectations serve as informative signals for principled backtracking. Furthermore, we develop a two-stage training framework that equips MLLMs with foresight-guided reasoning and efficient decision making. Extensive experiments on five long-video benchmarks demonstrate that ForeSeek consistently improves the efficiency--accuracy trade-off of long-video reasoning, achieving competitive or superior accuracy while observing $2.5$--$4.4\times$ fewer frames than the strongest search-based agent. Code is available at https://github.com/harry0021/ForeSeek

papers.title: Detecting Formation-Preserving GNSS Spoofing of UAV Swarms through Transmitter Parallax in Pseudorange and Doppler
papers.abstract: Swarms of unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) detect Global Navigation Satellite System (GNSS) spoofing by checking the drones' reported positions against their known formation. Formation-preserving spoofing evades this check: in GNSS-WASP, one transmitter per satellite, a few kilometres away, shifts the whole swarm while keeping its formation. We show that such an attack still leaves a trace below the position level. Because the transmitters are close, each drone sees them under a slightly different angle, and this parallax bends the signal arrival times across a 90 m swarm by 20-40 cm for a transmitter at 5 km, whatever delays the attacker applies. We propose a likelihood ratio test that reads this trace from the pseudoranges and Doppler every drone already measures, with all clocks and attacker delays unknown and no extra antennas. In simulations with real GPS and Galileo orbits and white receiver noise, 16 drones detect GNSS-WASP at 5 km in 13-60% of 10 s windows in straight flight and in every window during a formation turn with a precise Doppler receiver, where the countermeasure proposed with GNSS-WASP detects at most 5%. The same test also catches single-transmitter and ground-array spoofing.

papers.title: Conditional propagation of chaos for systems of particles with polynomial interactions
papers.abstract: We consider N interacting particles taking values in the real numbers and evolving in discrete time with time step 1/n. Each particle follows an individual dynamics, driven by its own noise, which depends on the total configuration via a polynomial interaction. Moreover, all particles receive the same collective perturbation. This perturbation is given by a multilinear homogeneous sum of order $ m \geq 2$ of independent centered random fields which are evaluated at the current positions of the particles. We show that, as N and n tend to infinity, the system converges to the solution of a conditional McKean-Vlasov equation which is driven by an additional Brownian motion which emerges in the limit from the collective perturbations. Moreover we give explicit bounds for the Wasserstein-2-distance. Our proof combines the invariance principle of Mossel, O'Donnell and Oleszkiewicz (2010), the CLT for Wiener chaoses in the Wasserstein-2-form of Ledoux, Nourdin and Peccati (2015) and a conditional law of large numbers for weighted U-statistics proven in this paper.

papers.title: The final stages of a Chapman-Jouguet detonation: support by its own products
papers.abstract: A planar Chapman-Jouguet detonation that runs out of fuel must become a shock. We show that, when the chemical energy decreases in the direction of propagation, the wave does not pass through the local Chapman-Jouguet states. The products of the richer mixture are at a higher pressure than the local Chapman-Jouguet state, so the wave is overdriven, it loses its sonic point, and forward characteristics carry the state of the rich products to the shock. The rarefaction behind the wave removes this support only if the distance travelled since initiation is small compared with the thickness of the fuel gradient, which is rarely the case. The wave speed instead approaches an envelope given by a Riemann problem between the rich products and the local mixture, ending at the Mach number of the shock transmitted into inert gas. For strong detonations this Mach number tends to a fraction $C$ of the Chapman-Jouguet value, with $0.621<C<0.625$ for every ratio of specific heats. The mechanism is purely gas-dynamic. Shock-fitted computations with a two-step chain-branching mechanism, for gradients 1 to 1000 induction lengths thick, confirm that no sonic point forms and that the induction zone never decouples.

papers.title: FrontierReplay: Split-Free Exact Prefix Caching for Hybrid Language Models
papers.abstract: Hybrid language models combine self-attention with recurrent layers whose in-place state updates restrict prefix reuse to exact saved positions. Saving states on a coarse grid wastes reusable prefixes, whereas existing fine-grained exact caches must cut the prefill forward pass at each mid-prompt checkpoint, adding scheduler steps that outweigh the reuse gains under load. We observe that across multi-turn chat, agent loops, document question answering, and tree search, prefix reuse almost always ends at structural boundaries predictable in advance, such as turn ends and known branch points. We present FrontierReplay, a prefix caching system that materializes exact checkpoints at these boundaries without cutting the prefill. While the forward pass runs uncut, FrontierReplay logs a short window of recurrent-layer inputs and invokes a cross-layer, state-only replay kernel to build the target state 6-37x cheaper per token than full recomputation without host synchronization. A frontier-aware retention policy prioritizes active anchors and proven branches while lending dead checkpoint slots to the attention KV cache. Across diverse hybrid architectures, model scales, and workloads, FrontierReplay delivers clear gains over existing exact caches, lowering median time to first token (TTFT) by 16-89% (up to 8.9x), raising 80% service-level objective (SLO) capacity by up to 1.73x, and improving goodput by up to 4.26x (3.67x at larger scales). Compared with approximate replay methods, FrontierReplay delivers up to 1.54x higher goodput while preserving exact task accuracy, avoiding the up to 17% accuracy drop suffered by approximation on long contexts.

papers.title: A Task-Level Bias Taxonomy for Historical Image Retrieval
papers.abstract: In recent decades, galleries, libraries, archives, and museums (GLAM institutions) have digitised vast amounts of cultural heritage material, including historical imagery. A major challenge in making these collections publicly accessible is enabling effective search and discovery. Many historical images contain incomplete, sparse, or no descriptive metadata. Consequently, machine learning (ML) methods are increasingly being used to generate or enrich metadata to improve the searchability of such collections. However, artificial intelligence (AI)-based systems can reproduce or amplify existing biases, particularly when applied to historical imagery. Factors such as differences between the data used to train the models and the historical images on which they are applied, degraded image quality, monochrome photographs, and historically biased or incomplete descriptions can reduce model performance and introduce bias into search and retrieval results. In this paper, we examine different forms of bias in historical image collections and review current methods to mitigate them. We investigate how these biases arise and how they influence AI-supported search and retrieval systems.

papers.title: Does the Workspace Do the Work? A Causal Protocol for Verifying Global-Workspace Computation in a Language Model
papers.abstract: Global Workspace Theory (GWT), a leading theory of consciousness, holds that information becomes conscious when it is broadcast to specialized processes that use it. Building a workspace into a network does not reveal what the trained network computes with it: a module that reports an answer may have combined a broadcast message with its own knowledge, or merely forwarded an answer computed elsewhere, and task accuracy and ablation cannot tell these apart. We introduce a causal protocol that identifies who computes when modules communicate. Its central test transplants a message from another input, chosen so that ignoring, relaying and recombining it predict three different answers. On networks built to relay or to recombine, the test assigns the right computation in every case. Among trained workspace models it finds all three outcomes: one leaves its broadcast nearly unused, and of two models that differ only in their training data, one relays and the other recombines. In AFGW, a language model whose modules communicate only through a learned workspace, a transplanted message yields the answer that recombination predicts in 97% of cases, and its content acts by redirecting what the receiver retrieves from its own memory. The tests carry over to other communication designs and to a known interface of a pretrained Transformer, turning GWT's central claim into a testable property of trained models.

papers.title: Charm and beauty production in pp collisions with ALICE
papers.abstract: Measurements of charm and beauty production in proton--proton (pp) collisions provide crucial tests of perturbative quantum chromodynamics (pQCD) and unique access to heavy-quark hadronisation. In this contribution, a selection of recent ALICE results, with emphasis on LHC Run 3 measurements, is presented. The transverse-momentum-differential production cross sections of prompt D mesons at $\sqrt{s}=5.36$ and 13.6 TeV and of fully reconstructed B mesons at $\sqrt{s}=13.6$ TeV are discussed together with comparisons to theoretical calculations. The rapidity dependence of charm and beauty production and the $\rm D^{*+}/D^0$ and $\rm Λ_c^+/D^0$ yield ratios provide complementary constraints on heavy-quark production and hadronisation. Measurements of the fractions of ${\rm J}/ψ$ and $ψ({\rm 2S})$ originating from beauty-hadron decays, and of the inclusive $ψ({\rm 2S})$-to-${\rm J}/ψ$ production ratio, further constrain the interplay between perturbative heavy-quark production and non-perturbative bound-state formation.

papers.title: Topology-Enabled Self-Verification of Quantum Hall Resistance Standards
papers.abstract: The scaling of multi-element quantized Hall array resistance standards necessitates rigorous validation that internal quantization has not broken down without relying on the verification of dissipationless edge state transport. One proposed solution is to use a Symmetric Precision Quantization Reliability criterion, a mathematical framework that statistically assures such validation strictly through outer terminal measurements of Cn-symmetric designs. This criterion essentially bounds the likelihood of hidden localized defects arising from quantum Hall breakdown and has potential uses in quantum computing and semiconductor testing but is presented in the context of its application toward quantum electrical standards.

papers.title: The construction of a regular non-Berwald Landsberg surface
papers.abstract: We construct a regular non-Berwald Landsberg metric of zero flag curvature on an open subset of the plane via a periodically forced oscillator equation. We solve the associated return equation exactly to obtain closed, strongly convex coindicatrices. Starting from a finite truncation of a formal control, we use a uniform local inverse for a periodic comparison operator and a smoothing iteration to make the return map of the original oscillator equal to the identity on the chosen base neighborhood. A direct calculation of the spray exhibits a nonzero component of the Berwald tensor.

papers.title: High-Order Area-Preserving Runge--Kutta Methods for Surface Diffusion Flow of Curves
papers.abstract: We propose a class of high-order area-preserving Runge--Kutta (RK) methods for the surface diffusion flow of curves, a curvature-driven geometric flow that decreases the perimeter while conserving the enclosed area. By coupling the parametric finite element approximation of the classical BGN formulation with symplectic RK time discretisation, we rigorously prove that the fully discrete scheme unconditionally conserves the enclosed area of curves. This conservation arises solely from the intrinsic symplectic structure of the RK methods, without introducing any additional constraints, auxiliary variables, or Lagrange multipliers to enforce structure preservation. To attain high temporal accuracy, we adopt $q$-stage Gauss RK methods, which are symplectic and yield order $2q$ (e.g., $q=1,2,3$). The resulting fully implicit, strongly nonlinear system is solved efficiently via an equivalent discrete formulation combined with a monolithic damped Newton iteration. Extensive numerical tests on various evolving curves validate the theoretical findings, confirming exact area preservation, high-order temporal convergence, and favorable mesh quality, while the Newton iteration count rapidly decreases to fewer than 8 per step, demonstrating the robustness of the tailored solver.

papers.title: Worldsheet Effective Theory of Abelian-Higgs Cosmic Strings beyond Nambu--Goto
papers.abstract: Cosmic strings can support long-lived excitations confined to their cores, opening channels for energy exchange with the transverse Goldstone modes that describe the string's motion. We derive a covariant worldsheet theory of their coupled dynamics directly from the Abelian-Higgs model at critical coupling, with all interaction coefficients fixed by the microscopic theory. The resulting action, which we validate against numerical lattice field theory simulations, extends the Nambu--Goto description to include a massive scalar shape mode and a massive vector mode. Dualizing the vector reveals a geometric distinction: the shape scalar mode couples to intrinsic worldsheet curvature, while the pseudoscalar couples to normal bundle curvature. These interactions explain the distinct parametric instabilities observed in lattice simulations and predict how the relative polarization of colliding transverse waves controls the excitation of the two internal modes. Our results connect microscopic string structure to the nonlinear worldsheet dynamics, providing a predictive framework for cosmic strings beyond the Nambu--Goto approximation.

papers.title: When Agents Play Differently: Localizing Human--Agent Behavioral Divergence with Conditional Distributional Testing
papers.abstract: Evaluating whether artificial agents behave like humans requires comparing not just average outcomes but entire behavioral distributions across diverse contexts. We propose a stratified framework that computes nonparametric discrepancy statistics within contextual cells, and discovers subgroup rules identifying where agent behavior departs from human play. We show that session-level metrics dominated by win/loss outcomes offer little signal beyond mean comparisons, whereas process-level metrics such as move efficiency reveal genuine behavioral differences. Applied to a commercial match-3 game, it uncovers patterns invisible to aggregate metrics: a playtesting bot is diverging substantially from humans in certain game modes, while showing no detectable divergence in others. We release our implementation as open source to support reproducibility and adoption.

papers.title: A Matter of Representation: Evolving Partial Spreads for Bent Functions
papers.abstract: Partial spread ($\mathcal{PS}$) bent functions are Boolean functions of maximum nonlinearity built from families of subspaces that pairwise intersect only in the null vector. We design an Evolution Strategy (ES) to construct such partial spread families, comparing two encodings: one based on generator matrices of the subspaces, and one based on spread sets. With the latter, combined with a ruin-and-rebuild operator, the ES finds $\mathcal{PS}$ functions up to $n=10$ variables. An ablation study shows that mutation is necessary, while the population size is not, and that a restarted look-ahead greedy heuristic outperforms the ES on the hardest instance. We investigate this finding with a landscape analysis of the stagnation points, and we also introduce a quality-diversity variant of the ES which finds $\mathcal{PS}$ functions of low algebraic degree for 8 variables. Interestingly, the bent functions evolved by the ES have higher 2-ranks and mostly higher degrees than those obtained by a baseline Genetic Programming optimizer.

papers.title: Lattice dynamics study of (Bi1-xSbx)2Te3 compounds: Comparative compositional study of force constants and Grüneisen parameters
papers.abstract: We performed a comprehensive Raman spectroscopy study of (Bi1-xSbx)2Te3 (BST-x) compounds, with varying Sb concentration, under ambient and high-pressure conditions. At ambient conditions, the frequency of all observed Raman-active modes (E1g, A11g, E2g, A21g) is blue-shifting with increasing Sb concentration, albeit with varying concentration-dependent rate. Based on these results, we calculated the relative force constants as a function of Sb concentration using a harmonic approximation, which shows a mode-dependent variation. The force constants for the lower frequency Raman modes (E1 g and A11g) remain almost composition-independent, while for the higher-frequency ones a profound softening (E2g) or stiffening (A21g) was determined. From the Raman spectroscopy measurements under high-pressure conditions, the corresponding Grüneisen parameters for the three observed Raman-active modes (A11g, E2g, A21g) as a function of composition were determined by combining them with the previously reported Equation of States and the corresponding bulk modulus B0 of the ambient-conditions R-3m phase. The average Grüneisen parameter exhibits a clear maximum for BST-07. Based on Slack's equation, these results are directly related to the optimal ZT values for this composition. Our study provides a solid framework for connecting composition, lattice dynamics, and thermal-transport behaviour, towards establishing the microscopic origin of thermoelectric optimization in BST compounds.

papers.title: Evaluating safeguarding in multi-turn conversations with AI assistants
papers.abstract: Conversational AI assistants are now used for personal and emotional support. Developers report improvements in how new models respond to sensitive conversations, yet users and civil society continue to raise concerns about their behaviour in real-world, repeated interactions that safety evaluations rarely capture. Often, evaluations present signs of distress clearly and in a single message, even though people may reveal their struggles gradually in otherwise ordinary conversations. We worked with three community mental health support workers to test if models provide the same level of safeguarding when cues are shared all at once or gradually over time. We designed nine scenarios in which a user shares cues related to depression, psychosis, or domestic abuse. For each scenario, the support workers established a gold standard response, ranging from signposting support to pausing the everyday task to address safeguarding. We presented five cues either together in one message or dispersed across a conversation. Across more than 7,400 conversations, we evaluated six widely used models from five developers. GPT-5.5, Grok 4.3, DeepSeek V4, and Llama 4 Maverick met the support workers' standards in just 26-59% of conversations when cues were concentrated, and only 3-6% when dispersed. Claude Sonnet 5 and Claude Opus 5 showed a smaller gap, meeting the standards in 68-97% of concentrated conversations and 59-87% of dispersed conversations. Even the best-performing model, Claude Opus 5, fell short of the gold standard in 13% of conversations when cues were dispersed. Safety evaluations centred on explicit, legible concerns can overstate how well safeguards protect people when signs of distress emerge gradually or indirectly through ordinary conversations. For claims of improved safety to be taken seriously, developers must design and assess safeguards around how people actually communicate.

papers.title: Fast X-Ray Transients from Dense Circumstellar Material Shock Breakout and Cooling Emission
papers.abstract: In this Letter, we explore the soft X-ray shock breakout (SBO) and cooling emission of supernovae interacting with pre-explosion dense circumstellar material (CSM) shells as a subclass of extragalactic fast X-ray transients. For geometrically thin CSM shells, we find that the SBO luminosities span a range of a few $10^{43}-10^{45}\,{\rm{erg}}\,{\rm{s}}^{-1}$, with peak times typically $\lesssim10^4\,{\rm{s}}$, both of which are primarily determined by the light-travel effect. When the shell's outer radius is located at $\sim100-500\,R_\odot$, the SBO temperatures fall into the energy band covered by the current soft X-ray facilities. We derive analytic lightcurves for SBOs in dense CSM shells and explore how different physical parameters affect the observed lightcurves and the temperature evolution. Despite the multi-temperature nature of the emission caused by the light-travel effect leading to non-thermal-like spectra, we find that the time-resolved spectra within the limited soft X-ray band can still be well described by a blackbody model. This provides a natural explanation for the observed blackbody-like time-resolved spectra of soft X-ray SBO events. Our model can reproduce the observed X-ray lightcurves and temperature evolutions of the three known X-ray SBO events, EP260321a, XRF\,060218, and XRO\,080109, revealing a diversity in the properties of the dense CSM shells ejected by stripped-envelope progenitors before the explosion. Future discoveries of more soft X-ray SBO events by facilities such as Einstein Probe will provide opportunities for probing the episodic mass-loss history of massive stars in the final stages before core collapse.

papers.title: System-One RSI: Building Muscle Memory for Interactive Agents through Guided Practice
papers.abstract: Reasoning models provide strong multimodal task understanding but struggle with sub-second control because deliberation increases decision latency. Fast decision models can meet the response window, yet prompting and few-shot examples do not readily provide the fine-grained experience required by a new task. Inspired by coached motor learning, this paper presents System-One Recursive Self-Improvement (System-One RSI), which couples two loops. The high-frequency online inner loop is an Observe, Orient, Decide, Act (OODA) cycle: a decision model maps each visual observation and task question to structured judgments, and a decision tree converts them into timed actions without invoking a reasoning model. The offline outer loop is a recursive improvement cycle carried out by a team of reasoning agents. The team revises the decision-model prompt and decision tree, captures interaction records, derives supervision from those records, and trains or deploys updated model parameters. The improved system then returns to the environment and generates the experience for the next round, consolidating learned distinctions as external muscle memory. The framework operates with a small number of real episodes, without expert demonstrations, environment modification, sandboxing, or parallel simulation. Experiments in Snake, Zenless Zone Zero, and Black Myth: Wukong use a 27B decision model. Mean Snake score increases from 1.30 to 7.35. In an evaluated scenario of Zenless Zone Zero, median completion time decreases by 8.4%. In an evaluated combat scenario of Black Myth: Wukong, the evasive policy achieves 11 times the mean survival time of a stationary reference, while the offensive policy win rate rises from 0% to 66.7% across the evaluated configurations.

papers.title: The influence of quantum scarring on the onset of Bohmian chaos
papers.abstract: In the present work we investigate how the stable and unstable periodic orbits of a perturbed two-dimensional oscillator influence the Bohmian trajectories of the corresponding quantum system. In particular, we find that in our systems all Bohmian trajectories become chaotic in the long run and examine the times needed for them to approach their ergodic pattern. We show that these times are systematically shorter for orbits close to unstable periodic orbits than for orbits close to stable periodic orbits of the same period. We demonstrate that this behaviour is connected to scarring effects associated with both unstable and stable periodic orbits. We also investigate how the Bohmian dynamics changes when a stable periodic orbit undergoes a bifurcation and becomes unstable.

papers.title: Flat bands and bound states in the continuum in non-Hermitian pseudospin lattices
papers.abstract: Flat bands support compact localized states (CLSs), whereas bound states in the continuum (BICs) remain spatially localized despite having energies embedded in the continuum of extended states. Here, we investigate the connection between these phenomena in a class of one-dimensional non-Hermitian lattices whose Bloch Hamiltonians take the pseudospin form H(k)=d(k)S. For integer pseudospin, the Hamiltonian intrinsically supports a zero-energy flat band and its associated compact localized states. When the effective pseudospin field has real transverse components and a purely imaginary longitudinal component, increasing non-Hermiticity compresses the dispersive bands toward the intrinsic zero-energy flat band, enabling their spectral overlap within a finite parameter range. The CLSs thus become embedded in the dispersive continuum and emerge as BICs. Adding a momentum-dependent Hermitian component along the gain-loss direction generally removes this spectral overlap without destroying the CLSs. We further extend this spectral mechanism to integer-pseudospin-n systems. These findings establish a connection between intrinsic flat-band localization and BIC formation through non-Hermitian spectral reconstruction.

papers.title: Extracting Value from Grey Literature: processes and technologies for aggregating and analyzing the hidden big data treasure of organizations
papers.abstract: Grey literature can be a valuable source of information about organizations activities and, to a certain extent, about their identity. Some of the major problems that hinder their full exploitation are the heterogeneity of formats, the lack of structure, the unpredictability of their content, the size of the document bases, which can quickly become huge. The collection and mining of grey literature can be applied to individual organizations or classes of organizations, thus enabling the analysis of the trends in particular fields. To this end, some techniques can be inherited from the best practices for the management of structured documents belonging to well identified categories, but something more is needed in our case. Obvious steps are: identifying sources, collecting items, cleansing and de-duplicating contents, assigning unique and persistent identifiers, adding metadata and augmenting the information using other sources. These phases are common to all digital libraries but further steps are required, in our opinion, in the case of grey literature in order to build document bases of value.

papers.title: AI agents can redesign engineering parts with more than a thousand CAD parameters and nonlinear simulations
papers.abstract: Simulation-driven design of real engineering components has to meet three conditions at once. It runs on few solves, since a nonlinear finite-element simulation of a 3D part takes hours; its design space has many values, the hundreds to thousands of values of the part's CAD model; and a better design often needs a redesign, coordinated changes of the part's proportions rather than local polishing of its surface. Automated optimisers meet at most two of these conditions. Classical optimisers, Bayesian or derivative-free, need a person to cut the design down to a few parameters, and on all the values they need far more solves; industrial shape optimisers move every surface node of the mesh in one solve per cycle, but only in small steps that polish rather than redesign. We ask whether a general-purpose large language model (LLM) can meet all three by joining what it knows with what the simulation shows. GPT-6 Astra edits a magnesium stent through a CAD geometry parametrisation of about 1,650 values, with a budget of 15 simulations; every proposal is built in CAD, meshed and simulated with large-deformation plasticity and contact, and the LLM reads the full results of every solve. Within that budget it lowered the objective, a high percentile of the strains in the stent's bends, by 32%; on the same budget, the industrial shape optimiser Tosca improved the original design by a tenth and then stopped improving. An earlier GPT-6 Astra design, 25% lower in the same objective, was checked in an independent, higher-fidelity model of the full deployment with crimping and damage: it was 14% less strained than the original after the full chain, and its most damaged spot began to fail later and carried 63% less damage at full expansion. LLMs can thus join their learned knowledge with simulation data to adjust more than a thousand design values and reach valid designs with real improvements.

papers.title: Critical nonlocal GJMS operator on odd dimensional spheres and mean field equation
papers.abstract: For a smooth axially symmetric function on $\mathbb{S}^n$ with $n\geq 1$, in odd dimensions we prove a neat formula for the critical nonlocal GJMS operator $P_n$ similar to the one in even dimensions. With this formula, we give a simple proof of the Liouville theorem by Gui-Hu-Xie (J. Funct. Anal. 2022): Every smooth axially symmetric solution to $$\frac{1}{n+1} P_n u = (n-1)!(e^{nu}-1) \quad \mathrm{on} \quad \mathbb{S}^n,n\geq 2$$ is identically zero, without using any delicate property of Gegenbauer polynomials.

papers.title: Moduli spaces of $(3,6)$-$K3$ surfaces and cubic surfaces
papers.abstract: We compare the ball quotient for marked nodal cubic surfaces with the arithmetic quotient of a domain of type IV associated with $K3$ surfaces arising from configurations of six lines in $\mathbb{P}^2$. Using the Coble map and the period mapping associated with the hypergeometric system of type $(3,6)$, we identify a common open subset of the GIT quotient of six ordered points in $\mathbb{P}^2$ and the ball quotient. This identification gives an analog in dimension four of the Janus-like phenomenon for the Segre cubic and the Igusa quartic, making precise a comparison suggested by Allcock, Carlson, and Toledo. For a related family of lattice-polarized $K3$ surfaces, we give a geometric realization of the ring of meromorphic modular forms with prescribed poles and trivial character and describe the corresponding Looijenga compactification.

papers.title: Xing-Audio-NVVASR: Scaling and Refining Supervision for Joint Recognition of Speech and Non-Verbal Vocalizations
papers.abstract: Joint recognition of speech and non-verbal vocalizations (NVVs) is hindered by scarce event-rich training data and inaccurate or missing event labels. We present Xing-Audio-NVVASR, an end-to-end recognizer trained through progressive data mining and iterative supervision refinement. Guided by unified acoustic criteria, two heterogeneous models cross-audit annotations, flagging disagreements for teacher reannotation. To uncover shared omissions that model agreement may conceal, complementary breath detectors screen the entire corpus for human review. Human-confirmed labels accumulate across rounds and are preserved during subsequent refinement. Over five rounds, we refine annotations for 170,000 utterances from public corpora and incorporate 630,000 mined utterances. The resulting corpus of approximately 800,000 utterances is used to train a single 1.7B-parameter model that transcribes speech with inline tags for six NVV classes. Across four human-annotated benchmarks, Xing-Audio-NVVASR ranks first among nine models in both composite score and six-class Macro-F1. It achieves a mean composite score of 64.46, surpassing the strongest comparison model, StepAudio 3 Chat Preview, by 6.03 points, and exceeds the annotation teacher's breathing F1 by 14.40 to 31.57 percentage points. We plan to release the model weights, inference code, four evaluation benchmarks, annotation guidelines, and evaluation code.

papers.title: A family of homogeneous convex non-scattering domains with analytic non-circular boundaries
papers.abstract: A homogeneous planar non-scattering domain is a bounded medium with a constant material coefficient that produces no scattered field for some nonzero entire solution of the Helmholtz equation at a particular wave number. It is known that the boundary of such a domain must be real analytic at all points where the incident field does not vanish. Previously, disks were the only known examples. We construct a family of homogeneous strictly convex non-scattering domains that are neither disks nor ellipses. The family bifurcates from a particular non-scattering disk, with the boundary, wave number, and constant coefficient varying along the branch. The construction uses a conformal change of variables and analytic bifurcation theory applied to the resulting nonlinear problem.

papers.title: Reinforcing Few-Step Diffusion Models via Shadow Posterior Matching
papers.abstract: Few-step diffusion models are widely deployed for their efficiency. However, reinforcing them with black-box rewards, as is routine for multi-step models, faces two structural challenges. First, a few-step generator is a sampler rather than a score model, so its velocity is not the forward velocity of the generated distribution. Second, it must be anchored to the undistilled teacher, which shares no transitions with it. Existing few-step RL methods handle the latter with a marginal KL to the teacher, but each pays for the former in its reward credit. We propose Shadow Posterior Matching (SPM), which renoises generated samples into shadow inputs and obtains the credit from their shadow posterior. From the KL-regularized reward objective, we derive a regression loss that turns reward values into a reward direction while anchoring the generator's outputs to the teacher and aligning the shadow inputs with the deployed inputs. Applied to 4-step generators, SPM achieves higher rewards with less reward hacking than prior few-step RL methods.

papers.title: Minimal primes and radicality of join-meet ideals of modular lattices with one diamond
papers.abstract: Let $L$ be a finite modular lattice with exactly one diamond, that is, exactly one interval of length two with at least three atoms. We describe the minimal primes of the join-meet ideal $I_L$ in terms of maximal closed distributive sublattices of $L$, and we show that $I_L$ has height $|L|-\mathrm{rank}(L)$. Moreover, we characterize the radicality of $I_L$, over any field, in terms of the complements of the atoms of the diamond in their fibres. Finally, we prove that $I_L$ is unmixed if and only if all its minimal primes have the same height, if and only if the rank of every maximal closed distributive sublattice through an atom of the diamond is $\mathrm{rank}(L)-1$; in this case $I_L$ is radical.

papers.title: Rational maps with at most three critical values have no Herman rings
papers.abstract: We prove that any rational map with at most three critical values has no Herman rings. This generalizes previous results of Shishikura and Milnor on bi-critical rational maps.

papers.title: Two-Timescale Channel Estimation and Port Selection for Fluid Antenna Systems With Limited Port Observations
papers.abstract: Port selection in fluid antenna systems (FAS) requires instantaneous channel state information, but a single radio-frequency chain can probe only a few ports in each coherence block. Existing FAS channel estimators, even with learned or generative priors, work within a single block and are limited by its few probes, which cannot resolve several propagation paths. To overcome this limitation, we propose a two-timescale channel estimation and port selection scheme that exploits the slow variation of the path angles. Specifically, a sequential Monte Carlo filter accumulates the angle posterior over blocks, while the fast-fading path gains are integrated out in closed form. Furthermore, a Fisher information analysis reveals that a single probe per block carries no angle information, whereas two or more spread-out probes accumulate it linearly over blocks. Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed scheme approaches the selection with known angles after about twenty blocks and, with four probes per block, matches memoryless schemes with eight.

papers.title: The Csisz{á}r order for ranking the importance of input random variables
papers.abstract: Csisz{á}r indices $S\_f(X,Y)$, defined as the $f$-divergence between the joint distribution of a general random couple $(X,Y)$ and the product of its marginal distributions, are widely used to quantify dependence between the input variable $X$ and the output variable $Y$. We show that the ranking of two input variables $X$ and $X'$ in terms of their importance w.r.t.\ the output variable, given by the comparison of the Csisz{á}r indices $S\_f(X,Y)$ and $S\_f(X',Y)$ depends on the choice of $f$. We introduce the Csisz{á}r order of input variables as the uniform ordering of Csisz{á}r indices over all proper convex functions $f$. We give a sufficient condition to prove Csiszár order of two input multivariate random variables. We fully characterize it in two cases: when $(X,X',Y)$ is a Gaussian vector (in the one-dimensional case this amount to compare the square of their correlation); and when $X$, $X'$ and $Y$ are Bernoulli random variables. Finally, motivated by sensitivity analysis, we show that, when $(X,X',Y)$ is a three-dimensional Gaussian random vector, thresholding $X$, $X'$, and $Y$ either preserves the Csisz{á}r order or makes the input variables incomparable; in particular thresholding never reverses the ranking.

papers.title: Holographic Tessellations Tensor Networks $\{p,q\}$ from Entangled Quantum Tetrahedron in Loop Quantum Gravity
papers.abstract: The relationship between spin network states in loop quantum gravity and bulk--boundary duality is further explored using the tessellated holographic tensor network. We develop a holographic tensor network construction based on quantum entanglement between tetrahedra in loop quantum gravity (LQG). This construction relates four-valent intertwiner spaces and Bell states dressed with $SU(2)$ holonomies to effective tensors on hyperbolic $\{p,q\}$ tessellations. For the $\{5,4\}$ tessellation, six tetrahedra are assembled into a single effective cell with five network legs and one logical index. Provided that the microscopic transfer map has full row rank, a right inverse and a completion on the kernel space are employed to construct an isometric embedding, yielding an effective tensor proportional to a perfect tensor. The construction is generalized to the $p=2n-1$ family, with local dimensions supporting absolutely maximally entangled states. On finite networks satisfying a radial orientation condition, an appropriate normalization produces an isometric bulk--boundary map. For cuts satisfying the isometry condition on both sides, the boundary entropy decomposes into a link contribution $\sum_{\ell}\log(2j_{\ell}+1)$ and the bulk entropy, thereby providing a discrete realization of the quantum Ryu--Takayanagi structure. Applications to the black hole interior are formulated via postselection-based non-isometric encoding. Assuming additional Haar statistics, this framework is used to analyze the preservation of overlaps on average and the competition between entropy branches underlying the Page Curve. These results establish a constructive link between the geometric degrees of freedom of LQG and holographic codes, while clarifying the conditions required to connect them to geometric area in LQG, the location of the quantum extremal surface, and evaporation of black hole.

papers.title: Revisiting Kerr-Newman-(A)dS Black Holes in \(f(R)\) Gravity: A Kerr-Schild Approach
papers.abstract: It is known that, in the constant-curvature regime, the field equations of $f(R)$ gravity reduce to the Einstein form with an effective cosmological constant, establishing a direct correspondence between stationary and axisymmetric black hole solutions in $f(R)$ gravity and their counterparts in general relativity, including the Kerr--Newman--(A)dS family. Within this framework, we revisit the derivation of these metrics using the Kerr--Schild approach for illustrative purposes. The Maxwell equations are solved independently of the Kerr--Schild function, allowing the electromagnetic source to be determined before addressing the gravitational field equations. We then investigate the possibility of non-constant-curvature solutions, taking quadratic $f(R)$ gravity as a representative model. Remarkably, the field equations within the Kerr--Schild ansatz force the Ricci scalar to be constant, reducing the resulting geometries to the familiar Kerr--Newman--(A)dS family. Thus, our analysis extends the recently established no-go result for uncharged black holes to electrically charged configurations within the framework considered here.

papers.title: From AI Surrogate to Engineering Tool: Toward Production Use of Fiber-Orientation Prediction in Crash CAE
papers.abstract: Crash simulations of glass-fiber-reinforced plastic parts are highly sensitive to the fiber-orientation field supplied to the material model. In conventional workflows, that field comes from resin-flow analysis, which requires molding-specialist support and takes about 25 hours of work per part. We previously proposed a surrogate model that addresses this bottleneck by predicting the orientation field in about 3 minutes. This paper reports the implementation, validation, and operational design that turned the model into an engineering tool for Honda design workflows. We present staged validation from 2D plates to production parts, evaluation against a predefined engineering angular-error criterion, and the expert review that approved design use in March 2025; the system has since been transferred to the crash-safety group and is in initial, limited use in directed fracture-prediction scenarios. The developed system combines injection-gate setting support for cases in which gates are unknown (90% gate-count accuracy, mean position error 11% of flow length), voxelization, surrogate inference, automatic mapping to the crash CAE model, and report generation in a single GUI. The complete orientation-preparation workflow takes about 0.1 hours, a 99.6% reduction from the conventional 25-hour flow-analysis route, and can be run directly by crash CAE engineers without molding-specialist support. As evidence of practical impact, component-level crash analysis using the predicted orientation field reduced the absolute peak-force error from 19.0% with an isotropic baseline to 11.4%, while confining predicted fracture to the test-observed region. The deployment lesson is that a surrogate model alone is not enough for practical adoption: gate-setting support, automatic data conversion, and shareable reporting are what make the model usable as a design tool.

papers.title: Asymptotic Bounds for Codes in Toroidal Distance
papers.abstract: The toroidal distance naturally describes the geometry of codes over \(\mathbb Z_q\), where distances are measured modulo \(q\). In this paper, we study asymptotic bounds for codes in \(\mathbb Z_q^n\) under the toroidal metric. We first derive an explicit asymptotic lower bound from the classical Gilbert--Varshamov bounds for the Hamming and Lee metrics, which serves as a baseline for comparison. We then develop a saddle-point approach for the toroidal metric, which yields an asymptotic Gilbert--Varshamov lower bound and an asymptotic Hamming-type upper bound. For \(3\mid q\), we embed ternary Hamming codes into \(\mathbb Z_q^n\) and obtain another asymptotic lower bound for the toroidal metric. In addition, we derive an asymptotic lower bound for Maximum Toroidal Distance (MTD) codes. We compare these lower bounds with the baseline and prove that they are nontrivial in the corresponding parameter ranges. Finally, we compare the asymptotic bounds numerically.

papers.title: Policy Improvement-Guided Replay for Continual Reinforcement Learning
papers.abstract: Continual reinforcement learning (CRL) requires models to acquire new capabilities while retaining performance on previous tasks. A stability-oriented perspective common in conventional continual learning emphasizes knowledge preservation and interference mitigation. Complementing this perspective, we revisit CRL for vision-language models through policy improvement, a fundamental principle of RL, to preserve acquired performance gains. Using the performance difference lemma, we characterize historical performance changes through the current policy's expected advantages on historical task distributions, motivating replay of historical prompts with the current policy. To allocate limited replay memory, we propose Contrastive Likelihood Replay (CoLiR), which contrasts likelihood gains on correct responses from the final task policy with likelihood reductions on incorrect responses from the initial policy. Our analysis links correct-response likelihood gains to reference-policy advantages under an idealized KL-regularized optimal update and provides an endogenous-reward interpretation for general policy updates. CoLiR estimates scores from finite training rollouts and cached log-likelihoods, selects prompts at task boundaries, and replays them uniformly during subsequent training, with KL regularization restricted to replayed prompts. Memory construction only requires a small amount of additional cross-policy scoring but no additional response generation. Across three Qwen3-VL model sizes on MRCL, CoLiR achieves the highest mean final accuracy and mean task accuracy among the compared methods while maintaining competitive new-task performance.

papers.title: Sequential Contract Design for Budgeted Crowdsourcing
papers.abstract: A principal wishes to crowdsource a collection of tasks under a fixed compensation budget. The quality of a task's outcome is stochastic and depends on the worker's effort level. Since this effort is unobservable, the principal offers contracts to workers specifying their compensation for each possible outcome. The principal offers these contracts sequentially, using previously observed outcomes and payments to decide whom to approach next and what contract to offer. The objective is to maximize the expected value of the work produced while ensuring that total payments never exceed the budget, regardless of the realized outcomes. Contract design must therefore account both for a worker's incentives and for the budget available to incentivize others. For valuations that are additive across tasks, we characterize how the approximability of the optimal adaptive policy depends on the numbers of workers, effort levels, and outcomes. Polynomial-time constant-factor approximation is possible whenever the number of workers, effort levels per worker, or outcomes per task is constant, but impossible in general when all three are unrestricted, unless $P=NP$.
