We derive analytical expressions for the time-integrated Rydberg populations to calculate the associated decay errors and also evaluate gate performance through master-equation simulations. Numerical comparisons with a fast Rydberg-antiblockade (RAB)-based CCZ protocol show improved gate performance at larger interatomic separations within the parameter regime considered. Monte Carlo sampling further quantifies the sensitivity to thermally induced position fluctuations. These results identify the tradeoffs between gate duration, Rydberg-state exposure, and interaction sensitivity, providing an analytically specified route to native three-qubit phase gates beyond the strong-blockade regime.

papers.title: AeroRSI: Recursive Self-Improvement for Aerial Vision-Language Navigation
papers.abstract: Vision-language-action (VLA) models enable unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) to follow natural-language instructions, yet still fail frequently in closed-loop flight. Correcting these failures requires repairs, i.e., actions that avoid them at the states the policy itself reaches, which human pilots cannot label at scale and rule-based planners cannot supply reliably. In this paper, we present AeroRSI, a recursive self-improvement framework in which an aerial navigation policy iteratively learns from its own failures. Our key insight is that a failing policy should judge its own repairs by flying on from them. Judged in this way, its sampled actions and even rule-based proposals that hurt it when imitated directly become reliable supervision. Moreover, an episode terminates at its first failure, concealing subsequent failures until the earlier ones are repaired. AeroRSI thus renews its supervision in every round, anchoring the failures of the current policy, verifying repairs by its continuation, and distilling them while keeping its behavior elsewhere. On TravelUAV, three rounds raise the success rate of a supervised 2B-parameter policy from 46.4% to 67.5% and reduce collisions by half, surpassing the previous state of the art by 10.6 points from the same initialization without extra human labels or inference cost. Code and models are available at https://github.com/starsholic/AeroRSI.

papers.title: Meaning Reaches Object Choice but Not Completion: Where Is a VLA Vulnerable to Landmark Synonyms?
papers.abstract: VLA policies are fragile to rewording. Success rates alone cannot say whether a policy fails to choose the object or to complete the task, nor where in the policy to intervene. We study the released GR00T N1.7 on two LIBERO-Spatial tasks differing only in the landmark word telling which of two bowls to take. Synonyms absent from the training instructions send the policy to the bowl they name, unlike made-up words, yet complete 67.6% of one task's closed-loop episodes, against the original word's 100%. Before the connector between the vision-language model and the action generator, replacing only the landmark tokens' vectors with the other landmark's (pasting) sends nearly every episode to the other bowl. After the connector, pasting at the landmark, the remaining instruction, or the image tokens alone rarely moves the choice, but any two do. Hiding the landmark tokens from the action generator after the connector still lowers completion for the synonyms that fall short. Finetuning on diversified landmark words repairs that one task's completion for synonyms absent from finetuning; finetuning on the original instructions does not. Training only the connector on the diversified words suffices, as does copying the connector of a policy fully finetuned on them into one finetuned on the original instructions. An open-loop score on starting frames misses that weights outside the connector also carry part of the repair. For now, on this evidence, robustness to rewording should be judged in closed loop, with actions executed, intervening on both sides of the connector, scoring choice and completion separately.

papers.title: Recurrent Domain Incremental Adaptation of Time-Series Foundation Models
papers.abstract: Pretrained Time-Series Foundation Models (TSFMs) provide strong representations for downstream classification tasks. Yet adapting a TSFM under changing operating conditions remains challenging. A model must improve on each newly observed condition without sacrificing conditions it has already learned, often from only a small labeled calibration set and without knowing the operating condition at inference time. We find that this difficulty has an important geometric structure. Under an operating-condition shift, the embedding space of a TSFM does not move uniformly: some local regions change substantially, while others remain nearly unchanged. Consequently, a global adaptation can unnecessarily move embeddings that were already correctly classified. To address this, we propose the novel PACT (Piecewise Adaptation via Chart Transport). PACT partitions the frozen source embedding space into local charts and learns lightweight residual transports for the regions affected by each new condition. An explicit identity path is always retained, and a learned gate softly selects among the identity and accumulated transports for each input. The pretrained TSFM encoder, classifier head, and previously learned transports remain fixed. With only 5% labeled calibration data per arriving condition and no condition identity at test time, PACT maintains an average macro-F1 above 0.95 across a four-condition bearing-fault stream. Under homogeneous tasks and label spaces, similar retention-adaptation behavior is observed across public benchmarks. Code is available at https://github.com/Sachithx/PACT.

papers.title: SemPhys: Semantic-Physical Co-Learning for Humanoid Motion Generation via Differentiable World Models
papers.abstract: In human-robot collaboration, natural language lets people direct a humanoid's whole-body movements without programming joint trajectories. A common approach generates a kinematic reference from an instruction and relies on a tracking controller to execute it. However, as the controller maintains balance under contact constraints, the executed motion can depart from the reference in ways that change the action it conveys. Our central insight is that semantic alignment must be evaluated directly on the complete motion the robot physically executes. Building on this insight, we introduce \textbf{SemPhys}, a framework that trains motion generators using semantic feedback from simulated executions. A differentiable world model and a fixed tracking controller predict a short segment of a recorded execution. SemPhys inserts this prediction at its original position, scores the complete trajectory against the instruction, and backpropagates through the predicted segment. A paired anchoring loss stabilizes adaptation by keeping each generated reference close to its counterpart from the initial generator. On BONES-SEED, SemPhys largely preserves instruction retrieval accuracy from reference to execution and achieves the highest retrieval accuracy on executed motions among the evaluated methods.

papers.title: 3D GameDev Arena: Benchmarking Coding Agents That Plan, Build, and Playtest extreme Long-Horizon Browser Games
papers.abstract: Coding agents now resolve repository issues and generate compact playable games, but whether they can build a large 3D game from scratch remains open. Such games tightly couple mechanics, scenes, assets, and interaction logic, and their quality rests on player enjoyment, which existing benchmarks rarely assess. Thus, we introduce 3D GameDev Arena, a first extreme long-horizon benchmark of 108 from-scratch game-development tasks across 14 genres. Given only a text specification and UI/UX reference images, a fully automated plan--implement--test--repair pipeline builds each task into a self-contained browser game. Runs average $\sim$1,000 LLM calls ; the longest uses 14,407 calls, 2.13B tokens, and 608 assets. Evaluation spans (1) objective code-level functional acceptance against the game specification, (2) agent-based QA and playtesting of 3D presentation and playability, and (3) blind pairwise Bradley-Terry human preference in a public arena. The preliminary findings indicate that long-horizon 3D game development remains far from solved, and code-level correctness alone does not dictate player preference. The public arena is hosted online.

papers.title: Construction of Ternary Minimal Linear Codes with Dimension $n+r$ Via Index Codes and The Access Structures of Their Dual Codes
papers.abstract: Recently, minimal linear codes have been extensively studied due to their applications in secret sharing schemes, secure two-party computations, and so on. Constructing minimal linear codes violating the Ashikhmin-Barg condition and then determining their weight distributions have been interesting in coding theory and cryptography. In this paper, we present a general construction of ternary linear codes of dimension $n+r$, where $n$ and $r$ are positive integers, and derive a necessary and sufficient condition for the resulting codes to be minimal. We first specialize the construction using index codes arising from spreads, with three classes of index codes satisfying the minimality condition, we obtain the parameters and weight enumerators of the corresponding minimal codes, and determine the access structures type of the secret-sharing schemes based on their dual codes. By the index codes from Krawtchouk polynomials, we then give a second specialization of the construction, with a class of index codes satisfying the minimality condition, we obtain the parameters of the resulting minimal codes, and determine the access-structure type of the secret-sharing scheme based on each dual code. Several constructed families of minimal codes violate the Ashikhmin-Barg condition.

papers.title: Measuring and Charging for Retained Context in Long-Context LLM Services
papers.abstract: Long-context large language model (LLM) services charge for repeated context, yet billing weights need not reflect its contribution to answer quality. We present a three-layer framework separating content relevance, observable proxies and auditable positional weights. Context-ablation experiments show that relevance dominates position and that distance-decay families do not outperform a relevance-only baseline. A measured serving stack shows that cache hits reduce repeated-prefix compute cost by over two orders of magnitude at 65,536 tokens, while cold resends constrain sustainable discounts. Cross-provider measurements separate cache value from tokenisation and list-price differences. Calibrated simulations reduce the 99th percentile of session charges by 31-42%, although revenue-matched nonlinear tariffs achieve similar reductions and median charges increase. The framework provides a bounded per-token accounting rule and measured deployment constraints, rather than a validated utility estimator.

papers.title: FDM+: A Framework for Constrained Control of the 2D Radiative Transport Equation
papers.abstract: Applying the frozen diffusion model (FDM) [29] to the constrained control of the 2D radiative transport equation presents several challenges. These include the dimensional difference between control variables and state functions, the resolution mismatch between traditional numerical solvers and deep learning models, and solution non-uniqueness. To address these obstacles, we propose a novel approach, FDM+, which includes three key improvements. Firstly, a decoupled prediction architecture is introduced to address the dimensional heterogeneity. Secondly, an efficient parameterization strategy resolves the resolution mismatch. Meanwhile, we derive a total error bound to analyze how the parameterization error and the model estimation error jointly affect the performance. Thirdly, the conditional distribution learned by the diffusion model is leveraged to perform design space exploration for multi-solution problems. A series of numerical experiments demonstrate that FDM+ outperforms existing methods in reconstruction accuracy and design flexibility.

papers.title: Polarized positron generation via laser-engineered quasistatic magnetic fields in a spatially extended herringbone target
papers.abstract: Polarized positron sources are of interest for precision studies of spin-dependent interactions and future high-energy colliders, motivating laser-driven approaches for producing relativistic polarized positrons. Here, we propose a scheme in which a herringbone plasma target organizes laser-driven return currents to generate spatially extended quasi-static magnetic fields. Three-dimensional spin-resolved quantum electrodynamics particle-in-cell simulations show that a 3.4-PW laser produces magnetic fields exceeding $10^6$ T, with opposite polarities on the two sides of the target and a duration exceeding 100 fs. A delayed 10-GeV electron beam generates high-energy photons through nonlinear Compton scattering, followed by positron production via the nonlinear Breit--Wheeler process. The resulting positrons exhibit opposite spin polarizations and deflection directions in the two magnetic-field regions, enabling angular selection of positrons with polarization exceeding $63\%$ at a yield of approximately $0.007$ positrons per incident electron, compared with a total yield of $0.029$. More restrictive angular selection can further increase the polarization to nearly $90\%$, albeit at a substantially reduced yield. These results suggest a route to polarized positron generation through the spatial organization of laser-driven quasi-static magnetic fields.

papers.title: Benchmarking Reasoning Reliability,Prior_Evidence Contrast,and Spectral Discrimination in Remote-Sensing Geological Image Interpretation
papers.abstract: Reliable lithology interpretation requires accurate geological recognition and reasoning grounded in visual evidence. Although Multimodal Large Language Models show promise in remote sensing, their reliability in geological interpretation remains unclear. We introduce HyGeoBench, a diagnostic benchmark of 10,000 questions based on hyperspectral imagery across three dimensions: reasoning reliability, prior_evidence contrast, and spectral discrimination. It covers ten task types, with both multiple-choice and open-ended response formats. Integrating hyperspectral satellite imagery with geological annotations and verified evidence, HyGeoBench examines reasoning errors, conflicts between geological priors and visual evidence, and cross-band inconsistencies. Evaluations reveal limitations in fine-grained recognition and evidence-grounded interpretation. To address these challenges, we propose HyGeoAgent, a tool-augmented framework integrating region observation, text knowledge retrieval, same-band image retrieval, and native PCA analysis through adaptive tool use. Experiments demonstrate consistent improvements over the corresponding base models, improving geological image interpretation across diagnostic dimensions.

papers.title: Adaptive Guidance for 3GPP Ambient IoT Contention-Based Random Access
papers.abstract: The emerging ambient Internet of Things (A-IoT) envisions connectivity among large populations of low-cost, energy-constrained devices. Supporting such connectivity requires efficient coordination of device access, particularly in reader-triggered operation, where multiple devices may respond to paging over limited shared radio resources. Indeed, simultaneous responses can lead to severe contention, delayed transmissions, and lost reports. This article explores how compact extensions to the current 3GPP Release-19 signaling framework could enable more selective and adaptive device access. The proposed approach allows readers to broadcast compact access guidance, which devices interpret according to their local conditions, while optional feedback supports continuous adaptation. Through a device-reporting case study, we demonstrate how such coordination can improve report delivery and timeliness under congested conditions, while highlighting the trade-offs across different network configurations. We also examine practical signaling considerations and discuss opportunities for more intelligent, adaptive, and resilient protocols.

papers.title: The Borel Ruziewicz problem
papers.abstract: We prove that for $n\ge2$ the normalized surface measure is the only rotation-invariant finitely additive probability measure on the Borel subsets of $\mathbb S^n$, and that for $d\ge3$ Lebesgue measure is the only finitely additive measure on the bounded Borel subsets of $\mathbb{R}^d$ which is invariant under orientation-preserving isometries and normalized on the unit cube. This answers the Borel version of the Ruziewicz problem. On $\mathbb S^n$ it suffices to assume invariance under a finite set of rotations with a spectral gap, and on $\mathbb{R}^d$ under two such sets of rotations about two distinct centres. The main step is a criterion for invariant finitely additive probability measures to vanish on null sets. For a finite nonempty symmetric set of homeomorphisms of a $σ$-compact metrizable space with a quasi-invariant Borel measure $m$ which is finite on compact sets, such as Lebesgue measure on $\mathbb{R}^d$, every invariant finitely additive probability measure on Borel sets vanishes on $m$-null sets if and only if there is $δ>0$ such that every countably additive Borel probability measure supported on an $m$-null Borel set is moved by some generator by at least $δ$ in total variation. Sufficiency is proved by constructing, for every invariant null Borel set, a bounded Borel field on the orbit graph, supported on the set and with divergence at least one there.

papers.title: An Updated Meta-Analysis of LHC Exotic Physics Results
papers.abstract: The replication crisis has raised concern across many fields of science about whether published results are as reliable as their stated uncertainties imply. Searches for new physics at the Large Hadron Collider offer a direct test of this for high-energy physics: those that find no signal report exclusion limits together with the limits expected in the absence of a signal and their $1σ$ and $2σ$ bands, which readers take to contain the observed limits with frequencies of 68.3% and 95.4%. Following a preliminary study in 2019, we test this reading for the ATLAS and CMS searches published between 2020 and 2025, 55 publications with nearly 400 exclusion plots, and reanalyze the publications of the earlier study. The limits are read directly from the vector graphics of the figures, and the statistical uncertainties are estimated with a bootstrap over publications. Averaging over the plots with equal weights, the CMS results agree with that reading, with $66.1 \pm 4.4\%$ and $95.3 \pm 1.9\%$ of the observed points within the $1σ$ and $2σ$ bands. For ATLAS, $73.3 \pm 7.6\%$ of the points lie within the $1σ$ band, compatible with it, while $99.2 \pm 0.4\%$ lie within the $2σ$ band, more often than it implies. Pseudo-experiments show that this can arise from conservative uncertainties, from the few events of many searches, or from expected limits computed after a fit to the data, the default of common statistical tools, which the plots do not distinguish. We recommend that publications state how their expected limits are computed.

papers.title: Toward Massive MIMO HAPS Networks: Antenna Architectures and Design
papers.abstract: High-altitude platform stations (HAPS) are expected to become an important component of sixth-generation (6G) and beyond wireless networks by providing wide-area wireless connectivity through massive multiple-input multiple-output (mMIMO) technology. As the communication performance of HAPS systems is fundamentally determined by the antenna array architecture, efficient antenna design has become a critical research topic. Motivated by these considerations, this article provides a comprehensive overview of antenna array design for mMIMO-enabled HAPS systems and proposes two novel antenna architectures to improve antenna-user alignment and communication performance. Specifically, the representative applications of mMIMO-enabled HAPS are first introduced, followed by the key design requirements for HAPS antenna arrays. Representative antenna architectures are then systematically reviewed and compared under a unified simulation framework based on the 3GPP NTN channel model. Finally, several promising research directions are discussed to provide insights into the design of next-generation intelligent HAPS antenna systems.

papers.title: Long lived QNM for multiple black holes
papers.abstract: We provide a rigorous definition of quasinormal modes (QNM) for the Majumdar--Papapetrou spacetimes with multiple extremal black holes. For certain configurations, the trapped set of the null geodesic flow contains stable (elliptic) orbits. We analyze this phenomenon in the case of two black holes of equal mass and show that it produces QNM converging exponentially fast to the real axis. QNM for black holes have been extensively studied for $\textit{single}$ black holes and this appears to be the first $\textit{mathematical}$ result for the case of multiple black holes.

papers.title: JEPA Dots: Dual-Latent World Model for Language-Guided Robot Control
papers.abstract: Predictive world models for language-guided robot control face a fundamental conditioning challenge: instructions should influence action selection without altering the predicted consequences of fixed actions under identical observations. To address this challenge, we introduce JEPA Dots (Dynamics-Oriented Task Separation), a compact dual-latent framework that jointly learns visual dynamics and language-guided control through separate dynamics and task representations. Language-conditioned task features guide a flow-matching policy, while masked attention restricts world prediction to instruction-independent dynamics history and supplied actions. In closed-loop evaluation on 40 trained LIBERO tasks, JEPA Dots achieves 84.9% overall success with approximately 39.1M parameters, compared with the published 78.7% of NanoVLA-S with 161.0M parameters under a different evaluation protocol. In the reference experiment, JEPA Dots also improves overall success from 76.0% for our task-ID-conditioned adaptation baseline to 84.9%, with LIBERO-Goal success increasing from 67.1% to 88.5%. Instruction-switching experiments further confirm that task representations and policy outputs respond to language changes, while dynamics representations and world predictions remain invariant under fixed observations and supplied actions.

papers.title: The ALICE asynchronous software trigger processing for LHC Run 3
papers.abstract: The detector and computing upgrades for LHC Run 3 enable ALICE to continuously acquire proton--proton (pp) and lead--lead (Pb--Pb) collisions at interaction rates of up to 1.5 MHz and 50 kHz, respectively. The resulting pp dataset is more than three orders of magnitude larger than the combined Run 1 and Run 2 samples, and its long-term retention in full would be impractical given the available storage capacity. To address this challenge, ALICE has implemented a physics-driven asynchronous software trigger designed to retain only collisions containing signals of physics interest. Following full asynchronous reconstruction, the Central Event Filter Processor applies more than 100 analysis-based selection channels spanning the ALICE pp physics programme. The selected collisions are then used to skim the original Compressed Time Frames (CTFs), preserving the relevant detector information within detector-specific time windows. This procedure reduces the retained CTF volume to approximately 4.5% of its original size, while preserving the possibility of future reconstruction with improved calibrations and software. This contribution describes the implementation and operation of the asynchronous software trigger, from collision selection to CTF skimming, and highlights how this strategy provides access to rare signals and processes across the ALICE physics programme.
authors: Sara Pucillo for the ALICE Collaboration

papers.title: R$^{3}$Sieve: Suppressing Unconditional Information from Attention to Answers for High-Resolution VQA
papers.abstract: High-resolution visual question answering (VQA) requires models to identify question-relevant small objects in high-resolution images and select the correct answer based on what they recognize, demanding fine-grained perception. Previous methods focus on obtaining better visual evidence (image crops), but obtaining it alone is insufficient, using it effectively is equally crucial. Visual evidence should therefore be utilized as effectively as possible throughout inference. We argue that small-target evidence is obscured by unconditional information that remains observable in subsequent processing even after the condition on which it should depend is removed. Such information hinders the effective use of small-target evidence. We propose R$^{3}$Sieve (Residual-Region-Response Sieve), a training-free framework. We divide inference into three stages---localization, cropping, and answering---and introduce distinct counterfactual references to suppress interference at each stage. During localization, the Shared-Subspace Canceller (SSC) uses a generic image description to construct a counterfactual reference and obtain question-relevant attention maps. During cropping, the Unique-Contribution Spotter (UCS) constructs counterfactual references from visual and non-visual features to identify distinctive, complementary crop regions. During answering, the Content-Aligned Voter (CAV) constructs an image-free branch to calibrate answer responses. Experiments on three high-resolution VQA benchmarks show that R$^{3}$Sieve achieves the highest overall accuracy among compared methods across diverse settings, improving base models by up to 21.5 percentage points.

papers.title: Replay, Don't Resample: Off-Policy Consolidation of Long-Horizon RL Experts
papers.abstract: Frontier post-training follows a common recipe: train one expert per domain with reinforcement learning (RL), then consolidate the experts into one model via multi-teacher on-policy distillation (MOPD). Such consolidation is expensive: the student samples in every environment again, an expert scores every sampled token, and the student inherits the drift of the final experts. Yet we argue that the experts' RL runs have already produced what consolidation needs: rollouts with their sampling probabilities and rewards, in the order the experts learned from them. We propose multi-expert replay policy distillation (MRPD), which replays these training logs through the student in the experts' order. At each step, the policy gradient is recomputed on these scored trajectories, and the final experts' distributions are distilled at the logged prefixes. Following the experts' own trajectory reduces the training-inference mismatch and keeps the student within the clip range, so the replay is off-policy in origin but quasi-on-policy throughout consolidation. MRPD samples nothing and calls no environment or reward model: the trainer is the sole process, and consolidating the experts costs only about a seventh of the compute used to train them. On three long-horizon agentic domains (reasoning, search and SQL), MRPD yields the best student model, substantially outperforming online RL baselines, and surpassing MOPD from the same experts at a fraction of MOPD's cost. Our analysis on the same logs shows that the replayed trajectories carry most of the gain, and that both the policy gradient and the distillation term add to it. Most interestingly, the order of the logs matters more than their amount or rewards, suggesting that expert training logs are a curriculum, not a data mixture.

papers.title: MIRAGE: A Framework for Multi-hop Reasoning under Dynamic Knowledge Injection
papers.abstract: Multi-hop Question Answering (MQA) requires large language models (LLMs) to retrieve and synthesize multiple pieces of evidence into a coherent reasoning path, which is essential for complex tasks. However, prior work on knowledge updating for MQA has largely focused on simple fact edits, overlooking a more challenging and realistic setting---\emph{Knowledge Injection}---in which the model must simultaneously accommodate both conflicting updates and entirely novel information. Under this setting, a hop-level answer is often wrong simply because the model trusts the wrong knowledge source: it clings to outdated parametric memory when the injected knowledge conflicts with it (K2), and it cannot answer when the required fact is entirely new (K3). To investigate this, we introduce NEXUS, the first benchmark tailored for multi-hop reasoning under Knowledge Injection, which explicitly covers both conflicting (K2) and incremental (K3) knowledge. We further propose MIRAGE, an efficient, training-free framework whose core component, the Correlation-aware Dual-path Reasoner (CDR), resolves such per-hop source-trust errors via P(True)-based confidence routing, complemented by a lightweight template-guided corrector for residual structural deviations. Extensive experiments across four LLM families and two benchmarks demonstrate that MIRAGE consistently improves both final-answer accuracy and hop-level reasoning accuracy, establishing a new state of the art in this challenging setting.

papers.title: Faster to the Wrong Answer: The Price of Local Updates in Federated Optimization
papers.abstract: Local computation can improve the conditioning of federated updates but may also introduce bias, causing their fixed point to differ from the global minimizer. We characterize the minimum worst-case bias achievable under a prescribed conditioning bound. We consider strongly convex quadratic client objectives with Hessian eigenvalues in $[μ,L]$ and local updates represented by a shared positive spectral filter. Client heterogeneity is measured by the root-mean-square gradient at the global minimizer. For a uniform surrogate condition number bounded by $χ\in[1,L/μ]$, we establish the exact worst-case bias per unit heterogeneity, $(L-μχ)/(2μL\sqrtχ)$, and show that local gradient descent with sufficiently small step sizes and proximal updates attain this bound. Our analysis reduces populations of arbitrary dimension, including noncommuting Hessians, to distributions over scalar curvatures. This reduction provides optimality certificates and worst-case constructions involving at most three scalar clients. We further extend the sharp proximal bias bound to smooth strongly convex objectives beyond quadratics and quantify the error introduced by inexact local solves.

papers.title: Action-Dependent Policies for Multi-Agent Linear Quadratic Regulation
papers.abstract: The linear quadratic regulation (LQR) problem over a multi-agent system usually requires a distributed feedback gain that is structurally constrained by the network topology, incurring an inevitable suboptimality gap. Existing studies either identify conditions on the system and topology that enable convex relaxation or seek a stationary point via policy gradient algorithms. In this paper, we reduce the suboptimality gap by adopting action-dependent policies (ADPs), where the control input of each agent depends on not only states of neighbor agents, but also control inputs of some other agents. We show that although exhibiting a distributed structure, ADP can enlarge the feasible set of feedback gains and even represent centralized optimal policies under suitable conditions. However, this comes at the price of losing coercivity of the cost function and possible failure of convergence for the projected gradient flow (PGF). To overcome this difficulty, we propose a partially regularized formulation, which guarantees convergence of PGFs, and forges a connection between standard multi-agent LQR and its action-dependent counterpart. Sufficient conditions for local convergence to globally optimal policies under PGFs regardless of regularization are also established. Finally, numerical examples are presented to validate the performance of ADP.

papers.title: Grading Executable Legal Rules Against Independent Records: Transitional Provisions and Korean SME Status
papers.abstract: Laws are increasingly turned into programs that decide cases, such as whether a firm was a small or medium enterprise (SME) on a given date, and large language models (LLMs) now write them. The programs are usually graded against answers written by someone who read the same law, so a program can score well by sharing the grader's reading rather than by getting the law right. LexTemporis grades them instead against records of what actually happened: 10,901 firm-years of SME status disclosed by Korean listed companies, with every version of the governing rules. An appendix adds comparison cases from US income tax and German hospital minimum volumes. The date changes outcomes mainly through provisions outside the main statutory text: one transitional provision raises agreement with the disclosures from 83-86% to 89-90%. The disclosures also test the author's reading of a contested provision, favouring it in 130 of 189 firm-years where readings diverge. Four LLMs wrote the rules, given different selections of the law. A pre-registered comparison finds no condition better across all four models. In exploratory analyses, supplying the right provisions looks better graded against the author's reading than against the records: the advantage shrinks for three models (for one, to between a quarter and three-fifths of its size), and per firm-year it is several times larger where the author's reading is wrong, partly by construction, since there reproducing that reading more faithfully must lose. Grading legal programs against the grader's own reading can overstate how well they work.

papers.title: Reliability of quantum communication over erasure channels
papers.abstract: Quantum information can be reliably transmitted at rates below the quantum capacity with an error that vanishes as the number of channel uses grows. The reliability function characterizes the optimal exponential decay rate of this error. For quantum erasure channels with a prime input dimension, we determine the reliability function exactly at all positive communication rates below capacity that meet or exceed an explicit critical rate. Notably, stabilizer coding strategies attain this optimal reliability throughout this regime.

papers.title: Odd-Even Effects on Liouvillian Spectra and Relaxation Dynamics in Boundary-Driven Spin Chains
papers.abstract: We investigate odd-even effects on Liouvillian spectra and relaxation dynamics in boundary-driven XY and cluster chains. With the bulk couplings and boundary dissipation rule fixed, the parity of chain length determines whether non-decaying oscillatory modes exist. Consequently, odd- and even-sized chains exhibit qualitatively different dynamical behaviors. We trace this mechanism to the coupling between bulk Majorana paths and the boundary jump operators. An isolated path supports undamped modes, and products of an even number of its Majorana operators span a non?decaying subspace of even operators. This structure yields nonzero purely imaginary eigenvalues of the Liouvillian and persistent contributions to bond correlations or magnetization after preparation in product states. The mechanism extends to cluster interactions of even range under a fixed boundary dissipation rule. The existence and frequencies of the persistent modes are independent of the magnitudes of the positive boundary dissipation rates. Our results unveil how chain parity controls the existence of persistent dynamics.

papers.title: From Data to Valves: A Self-Learning, Production-Grade Edge Stack for Sustainable HVAC Control
papers.abstract: Learned HVAC controllers rarely leave the simulator, and those that do are typically trained offline, frozen at deployment and retrained from the cloud. We present a production stack in which three learning components run on one NVIDIA Jetson Orin gateway per building, adapt continuously from the building's own data, and verify their own effect. (a) A compact transformer-encoder forecaster, one per equipment group with learned per-unit embeddings, predicts every air-side unit's next-cycle temperature and learns prequentially, one gradient step per five-minute cycle, behind five independent gates that bound the influence of any corrupt reading. (b) A distributional soft actor-critic agent, one shared policy across unit types, converts the measured state into a chilled-water valve position under a structural safety envelope that no learned component can soften; its second generation learns nightly on the device from recorded transitions alone, with a behaviour anchor and critic calibration terms, is scored by four model-free metrics and promoted by atomic hot-swap. (c) A change-point regression baseline held to ASHRAE Guideline 14 supplies the counterfactual against which savings are certified. On eighteen months of data from a hotel the forecaster converges from random weights within a week and reaches 0.37, 0.39 and 0.11 degree C MAE for air-handling, fresh-air and fan-coil units with no retraining event; on a different hotel the baseline reproduces a 46-day held-out period to within 0.07%. The RL agent has completed its in-simulator campaign and runs in shadow on 104 units; we report measured latency and memory of every service on a shared 15 GB device, the systems lessons of the campaign, and precisely what the evidence does and does not yet establish.

papers.title: Attention Is Not Relevance: Challenging the Causality of Attention in Autonomous Driving
papers.abstract: Attention has become one of the most widely adopted solutions for estimating the relevance of surrounding objects and interpreting an autonomous vehicle's driving decisions. However, its ability to capture the causal impact of individual input elements on an AI model's output has long been discussed in the literature, particularly in the Natural Language Processing (NLP) domain. This work brings this discussion into the autonomous driving domain by analyzing the accuracy of attention in estimating the impact of an input object on an autonomous vehicle's driving, i.e., its relevance. To this end, we compare different attention-based relevance estimation methods against a causal reference of object relevance obtained through counterfactual analysis. We perform our analysis on more than 80,000 synthetic driving scenes using an autonomous vehicle based on PlanT 2.0, a state-of-the-art Transformer-based model for object-level planning. Results show that attention provides a correlational rather than causal indication of object relevance. Attention-based relevance estimation methods do not consistently identify all relevant objects and tend to incorrectly classify as relevant objects with little or no impact on the vehicle's driving. In particular, results show that attention can effectively identify relevant objects in simple single-lane, straight-road scenarios, but its accuracy degrades in more complex settings, such as multi-lane roads and intersections. These findings highlight the limitations of attention as a proxy for object relevance, calling for novel methods able to accurately capture the causal impact of individual objects on the vehicle's driving and distinguish it from correlational associations.

papers.title: On p-adic asymptotic formulas for slope factors of L-functions of toric exponential sums
papers.abstract: Adolphson and Sperber expressed the unique unit root of the $L$-function of a toric exponential sum in terms of $A$-hypergeometric functions, whereas reciprocal zeros and poles of positive slope remain much less understood.We study complete rational factors of arbitrary prescribed slope in families satisfying a chain-level ordinary condition. Our main tool is a new contraction map arising from a twisted block LU factorization of the Frobenius matrix of a nuclear $σ$-module. Its fixed point produces an upper triangularization and the associated slope filtration, while explicit Schur-complement quotients of finite Frobenius iterates approximate the diagonal slope blocks with geometrically decreasing error. At a periodic fiber, successive cancellation in an ordered product of these approximations yields a quotient formed from two finite Frobenius iterates, and the characteristic polynomial of this quotient converges to the complete slope polynomial. Combined with the relative Dwork trace formula, this yields uniform $p$-adic asymptotic formulas for the complete slope factors of the $L$-functions of toric exponential sums. When the relevant slope blocks have rank one, the Schur complements reduce to ratios of leading principal minors and give asymptotic formulas for the individual reciprocal zeros and poles after cancellation.

papers.title: A Hybrid RAG Framework for Deceptive Review Detection: Integrating RoBERTa-LoRA, FAISS-Based Retrieval, and LLM Reasoning
papers.abstract: The growth of deceptive online opinions poses a critical risk of misinformation and fraud. This paper proposes a Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) system to automatically distinguish spam reviews. The architecture integrates RoBERTa with Low-Rank Adaptation (LoRA) classification, FAISS semantic vector retrieval, and a Large Language Model (LLM) for final reasoning. The system was evaluated across balanced and severely imbalanced real-world scenarios. Results demonstrate that five epochs of fine-tuning enable robust domain transfer, achieving an F1-score of 0.90 in cross-domain evaluation, outperforming baselines (OpenAI Detector,F1 = 0.82) and demonstrating competitive performance against specialized in-domain SOTA models (fakeRoBERTa,F1 = 0.97). The proposed architecture provides evidence-backed explainability and statistically significant precision gains while maintaining comparable overall detection performance.

papers.title: Turán number of the odd-ballooning of odd prisms
papers.abstract: The Turán problem for odd-balloonings has been studied for various classes of skeleton graphs, including stars, paths, cycles, trees, bipartite graphs, and certain 3-chromatic graphs. The Turán numbers and extremal graphs for odd prisms have also been determined. Motivated by these developments, we investigate the Turán problem for prescribed odd-balloonings of odd prisms. Let $k\geq1$ be fixed, and let $F^o$ be a prescribed odd-ballooning of the odd prism $C_{2k+1}\square K_2$, in which each edge is replaced by a cycle of prescribed odd length at least five. For all sufficiently large $n$, we prove that $${\rm ex}(n,F^o)=\Big\lfloor\frac{n^2}{4}\Big\rfloor+(k+1)n-3(k+1)^2.$$ Furthermore, the unique extremal graph is $K_{\,2k+2,\,\lfloor(n-2k-2)/2\rfloor,\,\lceil(n-2k-2)/2\rceil}$. The proof combines the decomposition-family method and Simonovits' structural theorem with local embedding arguments to establish the extremal structure and its uniqueness.

papers.title: The Shape of Individual Fitness Distributions and the Dynamics of Ecological Communities
papers.abstract: Developing a mechanistic understanding of biogeography and biodiversity that predicts species abundances, distributions, and fluctuations is a central goal of community ecology. We develop a model, that can be seen as an extension of Hubbell's neutral theory, in which a focal species competes with the aggregate of all other species in a local community of fixed size. Each individual has its own competitive ability, and the shape of the distribution of these abilities is incorporated in the model, represented by distributions rather than single species-level values. Under complete mixing, symmetric competitive encounters without ties recover Hubbell's neutral model. We further incorporate immigration from a larger metacommunity and derive a diffusion approximation for the focal species' relative abundance. The model shows that competitive ability distributions with the same mean and variance can nevertheless yield different patterns of local abundance. Thus, species that appear equivalent when summarized by trait statistics need not be ecologically equivalent. Our framework links individual-level variability to population-level persistence and abundance and provides a way to examine how competition and immigration jointly shape ecological outcomes.

papers.title: Optimal local gradient estimate for gravity water waves and its application to the Stokes conjecture
papers.abstract: In 1880, G. Stokes [Mathematical and Physical Papers, Vol. I] studied a two-dimensional gravity water wave and conjectured that the wave crest forms a symmetric corner of angle 2pi/3 at the stagnation point. The conjecture was first proved by Amick, Fraenkel, and Toland [Acta Math. 148 (1982)] and, independently, by Plotnikov [Dinamika Sploshn. Sredy 57 (1982)] via the Nekrasov integral equation. Their proofs rely on structural assumptions, including the isolation of stagnation points and the symmetry and monotonicity of the wave profile. In 2011, Varvaruca and Weiss [Acta Math. 206 (2011)] introduced a novel geometric approach and gave a new proof of the conjecture without relying on the structural assumptions mentioned above, under a local gradient bound for the two-dimensional stream function. In this paper, we establish an optimal local gradient estimate for general variational solutions of the free boundary problem. Our approach adapts the Hopf differential method of De Philippis, Hirsch, and Nahon [arXiv:2609.12180v2] to the gravitational setting, and combines it with their abstract approximation theorem to turn the holomorphic approximation of the Hopf differential into the local gradient bounds. An important new observation is that the weighted Cauchy-Beurling correction, combined with vanishing on the lower half plane, supplies the additional height decay needed to obtain the local gradient bounds. As a consequence, we remove the a priori growth hypothesis from the geometric analysis in [Acta Math. 206 (2011)]. For general variational solutions, we establish the Stokes corner or full-density blow-up alternative. Under the stated topological and interface hypotheses, we obtain the Stokes corner and two free boundary branches that are C^1 up to the stagnation point.

papers.title: Two-Color Coherent Control of the Spin Photovoltaic Effect in Centrosymmetric Crystals
papers.abstract: Spatial inversion forbids the conventional electric-dipole second-order bulk charge and spin photovoltaic responses in centrosymmetric crystals. Here we show that a phase-coherent two-color field at frequencies $ω$ and $2ω$ can generate symmetry-selected charge and spin photocurrents through an inversion-even third-order dc response. More importantly, the polarization direction and relative phase of the two-color field provide direct control over the current direction and can isolate transport channels in which the charge current vanishes while a finite spin current remains. A systematic symmetry analysis of centrosymmetric magnetic point groups and collinear antiferromagnetic spin point groups shows that pure-spin channels are allowed in a broad class of such systems under appropriate two-color driving. Furthermore, the relative optical phase governs both the magnitude and sign of the response. Our calculations on inversion-stacked bilayer 2H-MoS$_2$ and a centrosymmetric collinear altermagnet demonstrate resonantly enhanced, phase-tunable spin photocurrents in these complementary systems with strong and weak spin-orbit coupling, respectively. Our results establish the polarization direction and phase of coherent two-color light as active control parameters for spin transport in centrosymmetric materials.

papers.title: Accelerating Quantum Error Correction Simulations under Coherent Noise with Compiled Clifford-Augmented Matrix Product States
papers.abstract: Reliable assessment of quantum error correction requires understanding how coherent errors affect logical performance. Although tensor networks naturally capture coherent interference, entanglement growth and large qubit counts make repeated sampling costly. Here we develop a compiled Clifford-Augmented Matrix Product State (CAMPS) framework that reuses Clifford transformations across shots, recycles qubits released by measurements, evolves a compressed residual state, and accelerates sampling through rotation fusion and compilation tailored to the MPS layout. Surface-code benchmarks under fixed-sign coherent noise yield accurate logical error estimates at small bond dimensions, while random-sign simulations up to distance $d=9$ and on the $[[72,12,6]]$ bivariate bicycle code match the Pauli-twirling approximation results. Compared with uncompiled CAMPS, compiled CAMPS converges at smaller bond dimensions and achieves order-of-magnitude sampling speedups at equal bond dimension, opening a scalable route to studying coherent error propagation in larger fault-tolerant circuits.

papers.title: Compression Effects on Low-Resource Multilingual Translation
papers.abstract: We present a pilot study characterising the effect of post-training quantisation on multilingual machine translation quality and inference cost for three African languages - Hausa, Swahili, and Yoruba - across three model families: a small general-purpose LLM (Qwen2.5-1.5B), a larger multilingual instruction-tuned LLM (Aya-23-8B), and a dedicated multilingual MT model (NLLB-200-distilled-1.3B). Evaluating on the FLORES-200 devtest set (1,012 sentences per direction) under FP16, bitsandbytes INT8, and NF4 INT4 precisions on consumer-grade NVIDIA T4 GPUs, we find: (i) the specialised MT model outperforms both LLMs by 32.7-43.3 chrF on the Hausa and Swahili directions, and by 12.9-24.7 chrF on Yoruba, despite being roughly a sixth the size of the 8B instruction-tuned LLM; (ii) post-training quantisation preserves aggregate translation quality within approximately 1 chrF across all model families and language directions, with a single worst case of 2.19 chrF; (iii) on consumer GPUs, INT8 and INT4 quantisation provide substantial memory savings (49-61% at INT4) but do not reduce inference latency relative to FP16 - in fact, latency increases by 1.3x to 5.3x; (iv) a clear performance gradient tracking training-resource availability is visible across languages (Swahili > Hausa > Yoruba). These findings motivate a research agenda focused on hardware-aware compression and error-type analysis beyond aggregate metrics for low-resource deployment.

papers.title: CURVTON-205K: A Mask-Free Difficulty-Stratified Synthetic Dataset for Robust and Scalable Virtual Try-On
papers.abstract: Recent advances in 2D virtual try-on (VTON) have largely focused on architectural innovation, yet robust performance in diverse real-world conditions remains challenging. We argue that failure modes in VTON, such as inaccurate occlusion handling, unconstrained poses, and poor coverage of under-represented garments and appearance factors, are tightly coupled to dataset design choices and long-tail data regimes. We present a scalable data generation pipeline that coordinates specialized editing and generation models with vision-language model (VLM) guidance to synthesize triplets without requiring parsing masks or dense-pose annotations. Using this pipeline, we create CURVTON-205K, a curated synthetic dataset of 205K triplets: source person, target garment, and corresponding try-on image. CURVTON-205K is explicitly designed to broaden coverage across garments, person appearance, poses, occlusions, and visual conditions. Additionally, CURVTON-205K is organized into three difficulty tiers, enabling controlled evaluation under varying levels of difficulty and supporting difficulty-aware experimentation. We analyze the dataset diversity and demonstrate its potential to improve try-on fidelity across four VTON architectures and its cross-dataset generalization.

papers.title: An Isogeometric Collocation Solver Based on the Quantized Tensor Train Representation
papers.abstract: We introduce an isogeometric collocation framework based on the quan tized tensor train (QTT) representation to solve partial differential equa tions. The proposed method constructs isogeometric collocation operators directly in the QTT format using only a few sampled entries, enabling ef ficient compression and computation. The vectors of the geometry-derived coefficients at the collocation points are represented in the QTT format using the TT-cross approximation. We conduct numerical experiments using the proposed QTT-based isogeometric collocation framework for the convection diffusion-reaction problems in different spatial dimensions and for the Poisson problems on three-dimensional nontrivial geometries, showing significant re ductions in memory usage and computational cost while preserving solution accuracy.

papers.title: Stability analysis of stochastic differential equations with the Koopman operator
papers.abstract: This paper investigates the stability of stochastic systems through the lens of the Koopman operator framework. In particular, we establish the connection between the convergence properties of the Koopman semigroup and specific stability properties of the underlying stochastic system. Moreover, we demonstrate that specific Koopman eigenfunctions capture stochastic attractivity properties and we illustrate these results with two numerical examples. This work mirrors existing Koopman operator-based stability results for deterministic systems and extends them to the stochastic framework.

papers.title: A Capability Framework for Evaluating Agentic AI Platforms in Regulated Enterprises
papers.abstract: Agentic AI platforms-systems in which LLM agents plan, invoke tools, retain memory and coordinate to change the state of enterprise systems-are being procured faster than they can be measured. Public agent benchmarks score models in fixed harnesses; enterprises buy integrated platforms whose orchestration, memory, governance and tooling layers dominate outcomes, and they buy them largely on the strength of vendor demonstrations. We report an industrial evaluation programme ("bakeoff") run by the innovation laboratory of a global bank in which ten platforms-spanning open-source frameworks, proprietary products and hyperscaler ecosystems-were assessed by a cross-functional panel on nine capability dimensions across three financial-services workloads: counterparty credit risk, retrieval-augmented generation and process automation. Scores separate the field into three tiers that are stable under alternative weightings, and surface workload-specific strengths that aggregates hide. A secondary analysis, however, finds Cronbach's alpha = 0.98 across nominally distinct dimensions and rank correlations >= 0.93 with the total for eight of nine: a halo effect indicating that demonstration-based scoring measures presentation as much as capability. From these lessons we propose a gate-then-score evaluation protocol with four layers (capability, execution reliability, governance gates, business value), trace-level reliability metrics estimated over repeated runs, an autonomy-readiness scale and a reproducibility protocol. We state precisely what the present evidence supports, and what a controlled harness must add to turn enterprise platform evaluation from structured judgement into measurement.

papers.title: Semantic-aware Contrasting with Explicitly Disentangled Representations for AI-Generated Video Detection
papers.abstract: The rapid proliferation of AI-generated videos (AIGVs) has raised critical concerns about content authenticity. Existing benchmarks suffer from a fundamental limitation: real and fake videos are often collected or generated from different semantic distributions. As a result, detectors may rely on spurious correlations involving objects, scenes, or actions rather than intrinsic artifacts introduced by generative models. To this end, we introduce SAVGE, a large-scale semantically aligned AIGV detection dataset comprising 2,369,822 videos, including 424,115 real videos and 1,945,707 generated videos. SAVGE organizes samples into real-fake semantic groups by using captions paired with real videos as prompts for text-to-video generation, thereby providing both group-level correspondence and textual semantic anchors. Based on SAVGE, we further propose Explicit Disentangling and Semantic-aware Contrasting (EDSC), a model-agnostic training framework for learning artifact-focused representations with reduced semantic interference. EDSC first extracts and aligns visual semantic features with textual representations, and then explicitly suppresses semantic information in the artifact branch while contrasting real and fake samples within each semantic group. By integrating caption-guided semantic supervision with intra-group contrastive learning in a two-phase optimization strategy, EDSC encourages detectors to capture generation-related cues under matched semantic conditions. Extensive experiments on SAVGE and GenVideo demonstrate that EDSC improves most evaluated backbone-metric combinations, enhances robustness under challenging evaluation settings, and strengthens cross-dataset generalization. These results highlight the importance of semantic alignment in AIGV detection and validate explicit semantic-artifact disentanglement as an effective strategy for robust detector learning.

papers.title: FormalFixer: Intent-Aligned Automated Hardware Repair via Joint Refinement of Specifications, Assertions, and RTL Implementations
papers.abstract: Functional errors in hardware designs can compromise correctness and security, and must be fixed before tape-out. Formal property verification (FPV) provides strong guarantees by proving or refuting assertions, but a failed assertion is not always evidence of an RTL defect: the failure may also come from a buggy assertion or from a specification that is semantically correct but too ambiguous or incomplete for direct formalization. This creates a practical repair problem that existing RTL-centric methods do not directly address: the repair loop must align specification intent, verification intent, and RTL behavior before deciding which artifact to change. \textsc{FormalFixer} addresses this problem with a multi-stage, intent-aligned repair workflow for Verilog designs with assertions. It preserves the original specification as authoritative ground truth and appends confidence-filtered refinements to clarify implicit constraints. \textsc{FormalFixer} uses both intent mismatch and verifier-generated counterexample cone graphs to guide iterative RTL patching. This workflow explicitly checks specification--assertion--RTL correspondence. Results support intent alignment for FPV-based hardware repair.

papers.title: A Geometric Characteristic Long Exact Sequence for Codimension-Two Spin and Pin-plus/minus Bordism
papers.abstract: Following Botvinnik--Rosenberg \cite{BotvinnikRosenberg2023}, we define fibered-boundary bordism, introduce sphere-bundle bordism, and prove an exact sequence relating them to ordinary bordism. The sequence also holds when all sphere fibers are required to be non-$D^r$-bounding. Following Debray--Ye--Yu \cite{DebrayYeYu2026}, we define characteristic cycles with a chosen complement structure trivializing a characteristic class. For the GM and $\mathrm{KT}^{\pm}$ cases, deleting tubular neighborhoods and identifying sphere-bundle structures with determinant-twisted base structures give a characteristic exact sequence. This proves the bordism-group consequence of the DYY conjecture for our definitions, without constructing the conjectured map of spectra.

papers.title: Incidence methods for algebraic expanders over arbitrary fields
papers.abstract: Let $A\subset F$ be finite, $N=|A|$, $p=\operatorname{char}F$ (with $p=\infty$ in characteristic zero), and $L=1+\log(2N)$. In the range $N\le p^{1/2}$, we establish \[ |AA+A|\gg N^{129/85}L^{-72/85}. \] This improves the long-standing $3/2$-exponent bound for $AA+A$ in positive characteristic in the range $N\le p^{1/2}$, without any assumption on the multiplicative doubling of $A$. We further establish uniform expansion bounds with exponents $129/85$ and $32/21$ for four families of three-variable product--quotient expanders, together with refined estimates over prime fields. For $λ\in F^\times$ and $N\le p^{1/2}$, our four-variable bounds include \[ |AA+λAA|\gg N^{214/135}L^{-7/9},\qquad |AA-AA|\gg_\varepsilon N^{6681/4175-\varepsilon} \quad(\varepsilon>0). \] In particular, several three- and four-variable targets admit uniform lower bounds with exponents greater than $3/2$ in the large-characteristic range. We also prove bounds with exponent $49/38$ for shifted products and shifted quotients, and for quadratic-image sumsets when $\operatorname{char}F\ne 2$, as well as characteristic-sensitive estimates for $AA+λA/A$ and $(A-A)^\times/(A-A)^\times$. The proofs combine higher-energy inequalities, regularisation, and point--line incidences.

papers.title: Vanilla Adiabatic Quantum Optimization Can Have Subexponential Advantage
papers.abstract: We construct a family of objective functions $f \colon \{0,1\}^n \to \mathbb{R}$ for which vanilla adiabatic quantum optimization along $H(s) = -(1-s)\sum_{i=1}^n X_i + s\sum_x f(x)\lvert x\rangle\!\langle x\rvert$ finds the global minimizer in $\operatorname{poly}(n)$ time, whereas any classical algorithm requires $\exp(n^{Ω(1)})$ time to do so in the black-box model. Our result is achieved by replacing the linearization technique in an earlier work of Leng et al. (arXiv:2504.14841), which establishes a similar subexponential quantum speedup using a transverse field Ising mixer rather than $-\sum_{i=1}^n X_i$.

papers.title: Efficient Implementation of Diagonally Implicit Runge-Kutta Methods for Model Predictive Control
papers.abstract: In direct shooting methods for nonlinear optimal control, one of the major computational costs is simulation of the system and calculation of sensitivities. These costs are particularly steep when the stiffness of the controlled system prescribes the use of implicit integrators, amongst which, implicit Runge-Kutta schemes are most popular. These methods require the use of Newton's method to solve a moderately sized system of nonlinear equations with a dense Jacobian, the computation of which grows cubically with the number of stages, that is, the number of abscissa. To mitigate this we investigate the use of the family of Diagonally Implicit Runge-Kutta (DIRK) methods whose Butcher tableaux are lower triangular. We describe the structure exploiting linear algebra required to make the DIRK methods competitive with fully implicit methods, including efficient sensitivity calculations. Finally, we evaluate the performance of DIRK methods on several example systems, and show that the efficient implementation yields Pareto optimal integration schemes. The fixed step size integrators are provided as part of the acados package and use high-performance linear algebra provided by BLASFEO.

papers.title: Test-Time Symmetrization: Scaling Laws for Model-Agnostic Learning under Structure
papers.abstract: Test-time compute has emerged as a powerful way to improve the accuracy of language models at inference time, with scaling laws quantifying how accuracy improves with additional forward passes. Existing scaling laws, however, focus on repeated sampling from a fixed prompt, even though many tasks admit multiple equivalent representations of the same underlying problem. A graph does not depend on how its nodes are numbered, and a program does not depend on the names of its variables, yet language models can change their answers under such rewritings. In this paper, we study test-time symmetrization, which uses forward passes on rewritings of the input and aggregates the resulting answers over the group $G$ of rewritings. We prove that no amount of sampling and repeated decoding from a single representation can replace rewriting, while only $O(\log |G|)$ random rewritings suffice to recover the information provided by all $|G|$ rewritings. The same set of $O(\log |G|)$ rewritings provides simultaneous approximation across models, decoding rules, and sampled reasoning traces, and the logarithmic scaling is optimal in general. We validate the theory with experiments on Qwen2.5-7B, Phi-4-mini, Llama-3.1-8B, and Qwen2.5-14B, with chain-of-thought reasoning, on graph reasoning, logical deduction, and multiple-choice question answering. At the same number of forward passes, spending them on rewritings of the input is substantially more accurate than spending them on repeated sampling from the original prompt whenever the model's answer depends on how the input is written, and the number of rewritings needed grows only logarithmically with the number of possible rewritings, as the theory predicts. Our results provide a principled way to enforce symmetries at inference time when they cannot be built into the model, which we call model-agnostic symmetrization.

papers.title: Is It Worth Collecting Additional Covariates?
papers.abstract: In many studies, basic covariates are routinely recorded at negligible cost, whereas acquiring additional covariates requires expensive or time-consuming procedures. Thus, a natural question is whether it is worth to collecting these additional covariates. Using the reduction in prediction interval width as criterion, we evaluate and test the gain brought by the additional covariates and hence answer this question. We consider the gain both marginally and conditionally on the observable characteristics. The conditional formulation captures subpopulation heterogeneity and supports individualized data acquisition decisions. To avoid restrictive parametric assumptions, we adopt a model-free framework that accommodates flexible nonparametric or machine learning methods. We propose an efficient influence function based method, with proven theoretical properties to achieve our purpose under mild nuisance convergence rates. Interestingly, we find the natural conformal prediction based method cannot achieve the same purpose: It fails in the marginal case and imposes much more stringent or even infeasible requirement on the nuisance parameter estimation procedures. We demonstrate the superior finite-sample performance of the proposed procedures through simulations and real data applications.

papers.title: Scalable Vehicle Charging Coordination for Online Operations: A Column Generation Approach
papers.abstract: We consider an electric vehicle charging scheduling problem for long-haul freight transport. To mitigate unforeseen waiting times caused by congestion and limited charger capacity, we consider a coordinated scheduling approach that prioritizes scalable, computationally efficient scheduling for ongoing or online operations. We formulate the problem as a set partitioning model and develop a column generation framework with a label-correcting algorithm to solve it efficiently. We assess the scalability of our algorithm through both theoretical complexity analysis and empirical measurements, highlighting the role of feasibility and dominance pruning in limiting label growth. Finally, using freight telematics data from Sweden, we show that the proposed method computes optimized schedules for realistic instances with 1000 vehicles within seconds and reduces vehicle operation downtime by 78.6% compared to uncoordinated scheduling.

papers.title: Distinguishing Conserved Quantum Sectors via Measurement Record Features
papers.abstract: Conservation laws partition the Hilbert space of a quantum system into invariant sectors that are often difficult to identify directly. Repeated measurements on an ancillary probe, however, generate a measurement record that provides information about the occupied sector. Here we develop a framework for identifying conserved sectors using a $(K+1)$-dimensional feature vector of record statistics, comprising the average outcome frequency and pair-outcome correlations up to $K$ measurement cycles apart. For fixed $K$, the feature vector can be evaluated at a cost linear in record length. In quantum non-demolition measurement models, the average outcome frequency suffices for accurate sector identification. For an interacting spin bath with nontrivial dynamics within each sector, incorporating temporal correlations between successive and more widely separated measurements into the record feature vector substantially improves classification fidelity. Our framework provides an efficient approach to conserved-sector identification and demonstrates the importance of temporal correlations in distinguishing the underlying sector dynamics.

papers.title: Algorithmic Market Making Can Lead to Rough Volatility Through the Order Book
papers.abstract: Existing work suggests that markets can show volatility with paths rougher than those of Brownian motion. In theory this can happen when the order flow is close to instability with memory that decays as a power law. However, it is not fully clear how such order flow could arise from the predominantly algorithmic market making that characterizes order book dynamics. We show one such consistent mechanism. We treat each market maker as a desk that uses a first-order gradient rule to move the distances of its orders from the mid price toward target distances provided by an unknown oracle. We assume that distinct desks do not act synchronously in time but act whenever new information relevant to their respective oracles arrives, which each desk samples over its own characteristic lookback horizon. Across all desks the rule therefore takes the form of stochastic gradient descent (SGD) with information-driven (mini-batch) noise. In the continuum limit this update rule makes the volume of the order book follow a conservative stochastic partial differential equation (the Dean--Kawasaki equation) whose fluctuations drive the order flow. The distinct horizons of the desks further induce a persistent memory in the order flow that decays as a power law. Standard scaling arguments then lead to rough volatility. We confirm the key predictions of the model on simulated agents and on six months of Binance data with about 790 million orders. In liquid markets governed mainly by market makers, such as the perpetual futures of Binance, the order books are consistent with how our desks change the book.

papers.title: Boundary $ C^{2, γ} $ regularity for optimal transport potentials under the A3s MTW condition
papers.abstract: We establish boundary regularity for optimal transport potentials under the A3s Ma--Trudinger--Wang condition. Let the source and target be bounded, mutually $ c $-convex domains in $ \mathbb{R}^n $, $ n\geqslant2 $, with $ C^{1,β} $ boundaries, and suppose that the cost is smooth, bi-twisted, and nondegenerate. For positive $ C^{0,α} $ densities bounded away from zero and having equal total mass, we prove that both Kantorovich potentials belong to $ C^{2,γ} $ up to the boundary, where $ γ= \min\{α,β\} $. Consequently, the optimal transport map is $ C^{1,γ} $ up to the boundary. The proof extends the monotonicity formula method of Collins and Tong to general costs through the geometry of the Kim--McCann metric. The resulting formula yields homogeneity of blow-up limits and uniform estimates for sections. These estimates give boundary obliqueness and allow comparison with solutions of the constant-density Monge--Ampère equation, leading to the claimed regularity.

papers.title: Dynamic and Risk-Aware Procurement of Fast Frequency Response from Electric Vehicles and Heat Pumps
papers.abstract: Low-inertia power systems increasingly rely on Fast Frequency Response (FFR) to keep the frequency nadir above under-frequency load-shedding thresholds without oversized Frequency Containment Reserve or synchronous inertia. This paper proposes two complementary methodologies that interface with an existing day-ahead FFR capacity market. On the Transmission System Operator (TSO) side, a dynamic procurement rule maps forecasted kinetic energy and contingency magnitude onto an offline neighborhood-need surface, yielding interval-wise FFR capacity requests rather than constant seasonal or annual volumes. On the aggregator side, a risk-aware, TSO-certifiable bidding strategy quantifies reliable FFR capacity from fleets of electric vehicles (EVs) and heat pumps (HPs) by offering lower conditional quantiles of day-ahead headroom at a prescribed delivery reliability. The resulting requests and offers are cleared through a pay-as-bid capacity auction. A Cyprus 2025 case study shows that dynamic neighborhood-based procurement yields an annual clearing cost of about EUR 476,000, which is 30%-33% lower than the seasonal and annual static rules and also below the UFLS VoLL of EUR 637,500 estimated from the fifteen real 2025 events with fmin <= 49 Hz. EV and HP offers meet their target delivery reliabilities, and RMS validation finds 46 of 50 operating points above 49 Hz at both full and 85% FFR delivery.

papers.title: Intent Contracts: Taking Tools Away from Agents
papers.abstract: Intent contracts are an authorization interface for tool-using LLM agents in which the planning model holds no tools. For each step it submits a short logged contract: a goal, a verbatim quotation of the user, and scope fields. Code validates the contract, and a small trusted model checks it against the user's words and writes the tool call itself. Provided the validation and dispatch code is correct, every executed call is written by the trusted model, the planner's influence on a call is confined to a contract logged before it, and the trusted side decides how much of a request to carry out. We compare contracts with two reviewers of planner-written commands: one sees only the user's words and the command, the information boundary of a reasoning-blind permission classifier, and one also sees the planner's goal and a checked quotation. With gpt-6.1-terra as planner and GLM-5.3-Flash as the trusted model on three AmPermBench task families, every object changed under contracts is named in the goal of the contract that produced the change; under review the planner names objects in its commands and rarely in its goals. When the planner adds work the user never asked for, contracts complete the user's task in 27/30 runs and the intent-visible reviewer in 16/30, because a reviewer can only refuse a whole command. Contracts do not reduce unauthorized actions. They are indistinguishable from blind review, and once the benchmark's environment terms are clarified, every condition that changes state hits a wrong target in 40-49% of those runs. That error is the planner's choice of objects for an ambiguous reference, which no trusted model here can see the environment to check; telling the executor to decline when unsure does not change it. We evaluate benign over-reach with one pair of models, not adversarial planners. We release the plugin and run records.

papers.title: Geometric Decomposition of Entropy Production Based on General $f$-Divergences
papers.abstract: We construct a general class of excess--housekeeping decompositions of entropy production based on $f$-divergences for overdamped Langevin systems. The excess entropy production rate equals the relaxation rate of the $f$-divergence toward a relaxation target and also admits an optimal-transport representation, while the housekeeping velocity preserves the same relaxation target. Our framework recovers the Hatano--Sasa and Maes--Neto{č}n{ý} decompositions as special cases, and unifies their relaxational and optimal-transport aspects within a common structure. Moreover, our framework yields physically meaningful decompositions beyond these two by taking a desired distribution as the relaxation target.

papers.title: STAR++: A Physical-Aware Benchmark and Framework for Astronomical Super-Resolution across Multiple Filters
papers.abstract: Astronomical super-resolution (ASR) aims to reconstruct high-resolution star fields from low-resolution telescope observations across multiple filters for astrophysical analysis. However, developing a physics-aware ASR framework faces two challenges: 1) Data view: no large-scale benchmark supports field-level ASR, especially on unseen filters. 2) Method view: Existing ASR methods often fail to preserve stellar flux across spatial resolutions. Moreover, ASR requires reconstructing high-frequency components, including accurate star locations and profiles, making it more ill-posed than natural-image SR. To tackle these problems, we introduce STAR++, a large-scale benchmark comprising approximately 1.7 million flux-consistent image pairs across 36 filters, derived from Hubble Space Telescope (HST) observations. STAR++ uses a flux-preserving data generation pipeline to ensure photometric consistency across resolutions and provides the Flux Error (FE) metric to evaluate ASR models from a physical perspective. To address method-level challenges, we propose a Flux-Invariant Super-Resolution Plus (FISR++) model that generalizes to unseen filters while accurately reconstructing flux-consistent high-resolution images. Beyond the flux-preserving modules, FISR++ introduces two novel components. Specifically, a Filter-Aware Adapter (FAA) incorporates filter metadata to adapt image representations to varying spectral and optical conditions. In addition, a Spatial Ambiguity Disentangle Loss (SADL) models spatial ambiguity as pixel-shift uncertainty, mitigating the smoothing of learned conditional mean reconstructions caused by this ambiguity. Extensive experiments demonstrate that FISR++ consistently outperforms existing ASR methods in reconstruction quality and flux accuracy, while generalizing to unseen filters, highlighting its effectiveness for photometrically faithful ASR.

papers.title: Zeros of Pick and Hopf Differentials and Fences of Convex Domains
papers.abstract: We prove that the vanishing order of a Pick or Hopf differential controls the corresponding convex domain through sharp disk comparisons. For a complete hyperbolic affine sphere, Pick vanishing order $m\ge0$ gives normalized projective coordinates in which the domain lies between disks of radii $\sqrt{\cos(π/(m+3))}$ and its reciprocal. For a harmonic diffeomorphism to a convex hyperbolic domain with complete $\partial$-energy metric, Hopf vanishing order $m$ gives a disk in the image of radius $\log\cot(π/(2(m+2)))$, centered at the image point. Equality characterizes the corresponding regular polygons. For polygonal targets, these comparisons prove the Fence conjecture of Dumas--Wolf and give explicit Hilbert and hyperbolic distance bounds for higher fences. We also construct simple-zero examples showing that these sufficient multiplicity conditions are not necessary.

papers.title: Continuum: Boundary-State-Aware Deterministic Scheduling in Dynamic LEO Networks
papers.abstract: Low Earth Orbit (LEO) constellations support mission-critical services requiring bounded latency and predictable delivery. However, conventional snapshot-based schedulers discard the forwarding progress of unfinished time-triggered traffic across topology transitions, degrading schedulability and timing consistency. We present Continuum, aboundary-state-aware rolling-horizon scheduling framework.
