In one campaign, the system ran 1,097 completed candidate experiments and accepted 325, a 29.6\% acceptance rate compared with 15.6\% in the earlier campaign under a different objective and search constraint. Its best model increases search volume by 0.23\% in an A/B test of large scale. Several improvements were architectural changes the team had never tried, drawn from the broader industry and literature, suggesting that MLE agents can explore regions of the design space that human intuition overlooks. We find that the design of the harness around the model matters: intuition suggests that a stronger underlying model is enough, but in our experience, the design of the loop around it is just as critical. More broadly, our work shows that autonomous agents can do real machine-learning engineering in industry-scale systems.

papers.title: CoSlice: Coordinated Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning for 5G Network Slicing Allocation
papers.abstract: Radio Access Network (RAN) slicing is a shared resource allocation problem: each slice seeks to satisfy its Service Level Agreement (SLA) with minimal radio-resource consumption, while all slices compete for a limited resource budget. This creates both an intra-slice trade-off between SLA assurance and resource efficiency and an inter-slice conflict over shared resources, calling for specialized yet coordinated control. In this work, we present CoSlice, a coordinated multi-agent reinforcement learning framework for inter-slice physical resource block allocation in Open Radio Access Network (O-RAN). CoSlice uses preference-conditioned slice agents for fast resource allocation and an LLM-based coordinator to adapt their objectives using global network observations at a slower timescale. We formulate the problem as a multi-objective partially observable stochastic game (mo-POSG), establish the existence of a Preference Correlated Equilibrium, and derive a sublinear regret bound for the learning procedure. We implement the algorithm by using a two-stage training procedure that consists of multi-objective pretraining and joint optimization. We build a network slicing evaluation environment using ORANSlice and its radio-frequency simulator (RFsim), supporting realistic protocol-stack execution and application traffic across multiple slices. Experimental results show that CoSlice reduces both average and tail SLA violations compared with other centralized and multi-agent baselines under diverse slice workloads.

papers.title: Training-Free Domain Generation for One-Shot Federated Learning with Server-Side Pre-trained Diffusion Models
papers.abstract: One-shot federated learning (OSFL) has attracted increasing attention for its ability to substantially reduce communication overhead by limiting client-server interaction to a single communication round. Nevertheless, this limited interaction makes learning from heterogeneous client distributions challenging. Diffusion-based OSFL approaches seek to address this challenge by synthesizing data that approximate client distributions. However, existing diffusion-based approaches often impose substantial computational costs on clients and lack effective visual guidance to generate data aligned with client distributions. To address these limitations, we propose FedDoG, a training-free Domain Generation framework that leverages server-side pre-trained diffusion models to synthesize data aligned with client domains. FedDoG extracts compact domain representations using a frozen image encoder, substantially reducing client-side computational and communication costs. These representations are incorporated into the diffusion model through a pre-trained image-conditioning adapter, thereby providing explicit visual guidance for domain generation. To further improve the quality of synthetic data, FedDoG adapts the strength of visual conditioning according to domain concentration and filters generated samples based on class consistency and predictive entropy. Experiments on three benchmarks demonstrate that FedDoG generates higher-quality synthetic images and outperforms existing OSFL baselines in classification accuracy. Meanwhile, FedDoG reduces client upload and computation time by 99.9% and 91.5%, respectively. The code is available at https://github.com/YXTong17/FedDoG.

papers.title: Evaluating invariance training with certified answer-changing controls in neural graph algorithms
papers.abstract: Invariance training aims to make neural algorithmic reasoners robust to answer-preserving input changes and is judged by accuracy and by how rarely such edits change predictions. We ask whether this evaluation detects lost sensitivity to answer-changing edits on minimum spanning trees of synthetic graphs, where both directions can be certified. Attaching a subgraph through one bridge provably preserves every original label. Attaching it through two edges, oracle-selected to change a label, and lowering one weight inside the graph serve as answer-changing controls; a response is a changed prediction on an edge whose label changes. A reproduced graph transformer (GDT) within its published accuracy range changes a provably fixed label on 53.3-65.9% of the 64-vertex graphs it solves exactly after a 64-vertex bridge attachment; removing the connecting edge changes little. With 16-vertex graphs and attachments, three invariance objectives lower GDT violations from 2.91% to 0.52-2.02% of pairs at essentially unchanged accuracy. Training also lowers the response to two-edge attachments from 97.6% to 66.0-79.0%, while the response to in-base weight edits stays near 99.5%. At 64 vertices accuracy also falls, but on 16-vertex bases only the attachment control reveals the loss. A message-passing network loses some attachment response at small penalty weights but gains little invariance. Running the conventionally trained GDT on each biconnected block separately removes all observed violations and keeps accuracy and both responses, so the task does not force the trade-off. Sensitivity checks for trained invariance should include certified answer-changing edits that attach material as the training edits do.

papers.title: Inverse Reconstruction of Two-Field Potentials for a DESI-Motivated Phantom-Divide Transition
papers.abstract: A phantom-divide transition favored by recent cosmological observations poses an inverse problem: which field potentials realize the inferred expansion history, and what features are uniquely fixed by it? We reconstruct local potentials for a canonical-phantom scalar pair with standard matter and radiation, targeting Metastable Emergent Dark Energy histories constrained by CMB, DESI BAO, and Type Ia supernova data. The coupled-field Friedmann evolution reproduces the target background to numerical accuracy across the transition, with regular perturbations through the crossing. At the phantom divide, the transition slope sets a dimensionless potential-energy release rate insensitive to the partition of kinetic energy. We identify local potential deformations that preserve both background expansion and linear dynamics. This construction gives a classical field realization of the inferred transition and disentangles observationally fixed energy balances from interaction terms requiring additional theoretical input.

papers.title: Inference-Time Scaling in Agentic Hardware Verification Workflows: A Multi-Strategy Characterization Across Protocol Complexity
papers.abstract: Inference-time scaling, allocating more compute during generation rather than pre-training, has demonstrated dramatic quality improvements for LLM reasoning tasks. Its behaviour in structured hardware verification code generation, where outputs must satisfy compiler correctness, protocol semantics, and functional coverage constraints simultaneously, is less understood. We present a systematic, simulator-grounded study of inference-time compute scaling for agentic UVM testbench synthesis targeting AMBA protocol bridges. Four inference strategies---zero-shot (\$0.04), raw-feedback iterative (\$0.81), structured inner-loop (\$0.95), and full dual-loop agentic synthesis (\$1.06)---are evaluated across four AMBA targets (Protocol Complexity Index 11.8--22.6) using the Protocol Verification Completeness (PVC) metric, functional coverage, and a six-class UVM error taxonomy (E1--E6). Our central finding is that structured diagnostic feedback acts as an inference-time compute multiplier: the structured inner loop yields roughly $15\times$ more PVC per inference dollar than raw EDA-tool feedback (marginal efficiency, S1$\to$S2 vs. S0$\to$S1). The mechanism is fault targeting, not token reduction: raw compiler feedback drives the testbench to compile but cannot surface functional protocol faults that leave the code syntactically valid, whereas structured E1--E6 bundles diagnose and resolve them. All outputs are judged by a cycle-accurate Mentor Questa toolchain rather than by model self-assessment; the dual-loop strategy reaches PVC $\geq$ 0.95 with zero scoreboard errors on every target, and the generated environments surfaced a latent RTL bug in two of the four reference designs. These results establish a principled compute-quality trade-off curve for LLM-aided verification environment generation and motivate inference-budget-aware deployment strategies for industrial EDA workflows.

papers.title: MIMO Channel Extrapolation to Unobserved Radiation Modes via Learned Path Refinement
papers.abstract: A pattern-reconfigurable multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) receiver can sample every antenna element and still leave entire radiation modes unobserved. The calibrated patterns weight a common set of propagation paths, which links these missing channels to the measured rows. Our estimator learns to correct the complex gains and spatial frequencies of those paths, so a correction inferred from measured rows updates every unmeasured mode. Each stage combines a damped least-squares proposal with a learned correction scaled by noise power and local array sensitivity. Training on complete simulated channels rewards corrections that reduce prediction error across modes, including those with no measured rows. The learned rule transfers from pursuit-based training estimates to a ridge variable-projection initializer without retraining. In matched simulations, refinement reduces error on wholly unobserved modes as well as across the full channel. Coefficient updates account for most of the gain, and the learned rule further improves on adaptive ridge shrinkage at fixed angles. Individual channel trajectories show that extrapolation can improve even as the residual on the measured rows increases.

papers.title: AI Surge Accelerates the Transition to Liquid Cooling: Rethinking Energy and Water Use in Data Center Cooling
papers.abstract: The power density of AI workloads is rapidly driving shifts to liquid cooling. This study rethinks and assesses the global impact on energy and water demand of this cooling transformation. Results suggest that liquid cooling can reduce cooling energy use by 25-56% relative to air cooling, offering substantial energy savings for GW-scale AI data centers. Best-practice PUE values could be as low as 1.07-1.08 for today's systems and 1.03-1.04 for emerging designs, and WUE values range from 0.38 to 2.63 L/kWh, depending on temperature conditions. We identify global free-cooling rack inlet temperature thresholds of 33 $^\circ$C for evaporative systems and 49 $^\circ$C for dry systems, demonstrating the practicality of 100% free cooling in many locations. The model finds that minimum PUEs do not necessarily coincide with minimum total energy use, because warmer coolant raises server power. Results quantify the large sustainability potential of liquid cooling and provide actionable targets for data center design and policies.

papers.title: Constructive Trend to Equilibrium for Low-regularity Boltzmann and BGK equations
papers.abstract: We study the long-time behavior of global mild solutions to the cutoff Boltzmann and BGK equations on $\T^3$ under a Gaussian lower bound and a polynomially weighted $L^\infty$ upper bound. The main step is a finite-time estimate which uses free transport to control the entropy of the local Maxwellian by microscopic entropy and dissipation, without assuming Sobolev regularity. For Boltzmann, Villani's entropy-production inequality and a comparison of collision kernels give polynomial decay when the velocity weight has order $m>7$. For a sufficiently large weight, the large-amplitude theory then gives exponential decay in the weighted norm and in relative entropy. For BGK, the microscopic inequality is linear, so entropy decays exponentially from the finite-time estimate. Finally, we establish a density criterion for large-data BGK dynamics in the polynomially weighted $L^\infty$ class of Perthame and Pulvirenti. For weight order $m>10$, a uniform upper bound on the local density guarantees uniform-in-time weighted bounds and exponential convergence to equilibrium in both relative entropy and the weighted $L^\infty$ norm.

papers.title: On global error estimates of a local discontinuous Galerkin method of the Boussinesq system of equations
papers.abstract: In this paper, we develop and analyze a local discontinuous Galerkin (LDG) finite element method for the Boussinesq system of equations, and employ an upwind scheme to effectively manage the nonlinear convective terms, thereby ensuring stability and accuracy. Our analysis establishes new \emph{a priori} regularity estimates for the semidiscrete LDG approximations. We establish optimal \emph{a priori} error estimates for the velocity approximation in $\bL^2$--norm, the pressure approximation in $L^2$--norm and for temperature in $L^2$--norm for all $t>0$. Our proof relies on the standard elliptic and parabolic duality arguments and modified Stokes operators defined on appropriate broken Sobolev spaces. Under suitable smallness assumptions on the given data, we further establish error estimates that remain uniform in time. Furthermore, the backward Euler scheme is considered for a full discretization, and optimal fully discrete error estimates are derived. Finally, we carry out numerical experiments to substantiate our theoretical findings.

papers.title: Coverage Governs Accuracy: When to Expand the Lexicon and When to Fall Back in Low-Resource Manchu OCR
papers.abstract: Character-level OCR for low-resource Manchu often produces near-miss spelling errors. Lexicon-constrained decoding can correct such errors with lexical knowledge, but a fixed dictionary cannot cover the many unseen word forms produced by agglutinative word formation. We study whether morphological expansion alleviates this limitation, and how the expansion size and confidence fallback affect recognition. We segment the training transcriptions with a dictionary-based stem list, extract roots and suffix chains from them, generate about 510k candidates, select the expansion size through frequency ranking on the validation set, and decompose accuracy under hard lexicon constraints into the product of coverage and in-lexicon precision. Across three CRNN training seeds, adding 250k candidates to a base dictionary of about 29k words raises the type accuracy on unseen combinations of seen roots from 63.6% to 86.3%, and overall token accuracy from 82.4% to 84.2%. Adding all candidates lowers overall token accuracy to 81.5%, showing that the coverage gain comes with a loss of in-lexicon precision. A further comparison shows that the base dictionary with confidence fallback performs best overall among the CRNN systems tested, reaching 76.1% type and 85.5% token accuracy and outperforming the expanded lexicon both with and without fallback. A Transformer recognizer shows similar trends. These results indicate that morphological expansion relieves the constraint of a fixed dictionary, but a larger lexicon does not guarantee better recognition; in the present low-resource Manchu OCR setting, a selective combination of reliable lexical constraints and open recognition is more effective.

papers.title: Categorified Koszul duality and deformation theory of higher categories
papers.abstract: This paper develops a deformation theory for stable $(\infty,n)$-categories for $n > 1$. We introduce the framework of complete $t$-structured stable presentable $(\infty,n)$-categories. Within this setting, we establish a higher categorified Koszul duality among complete $t$-structured presentable $(\infty,n)$-categories. Using this duality, we develop the deformation theory. We prove that the deformation problem for such categories is a well-behaved formal moduli problem determined by Hochschild cohomology, and we deduce the corresponding obstruction theory. Finally, we apply our results to sheaves of categories on perfect stacks.

papers.title: Cascadeability and the Realization Gap: An Empirical Study of LLM-Powered Semantic Filtering
papers.abstract: Semantic filters enable natural language predicates over unstructured documents, but evaluating every document with a large language model (LLM) oracle is expensive. Proxy cascades reduce oracle invocations using cheaper surrogates, but oracle reduction alone cannot distinguish proxy limitations from calibration bottlenecks and establish practical efficiency. We present a unified benchmark of four representative systems, which formulate query processing as a three-stage workflow comprising proxy construction, threshold calibration, and cascade inference, using a two-threshold acceptance rule. We introduce cascadeability: the maximum empirical oracle reduction attainable from fixed proxy scores at a specified accuracy target, computed retrospectively using complete oracle labels. We investigate 8 research questions, spanning proxy quality, end-to-end performance, workload sensitivities, and component ablations, and reveal our key findings accordingly. Comparing cascadeability with achieved oracle reduction yields a realization gap that, interpreted alongside accuracy, exposes distinct proxy and calibration bottlenecks. The benchmark and diagnostics support evaluation beyond oracle reduction and motivate joint proxy-calibration design, class-sensitive quality assessment, and end-to-end cost optimization. We release a dataset-query benchmark, containing 10 real-world workloads across various domains and difficulties, with annotations of two LLM families.

papers.title: Projected Sensitivity of a Differential Torsion Sensor for Tests of the Weak Equivalence Principle
papers.abstract: Tests of the weak equivalence principle (WEP) are among the most sensitive probes of new long-range, composition-dependent interactions beyond general relativity and the Standard Model. We evaluate the potential of a differential torsion sensor, which combines long mechanical coherence times with optical-cavity readout and common-mode rejection, for laboratory WEP tests and fifth-force searches. For a representative configuration based on an existing prototype, with Be-Ti test masses and 180 days of coherent integration, the projected noise-limited sensitivity to the Eötvös parameter is $η\simeq7.5\times10^{-16}$ and $2.4\times10^{-16}$ for signal modulation at 2 and 20 mHz, respectively, below current ground-based torsion-balance limits. For a baryon-coupled Yukawa interaction sourced by the Earth, the corresponding projected sensitivity to the coupling strength is $α\simeq3.1\times10^{-13}$ and $9.8\times10^{-14}$ for ranges $λ\gtrsim10^{7}$ m. We identify the modulation scheme, the material contrast, and the source geometry as the main factors that set the projected reach, and the control of systematic couplings as the main experimental requirement for attaining it. These results indicate that differential torsion sensors are a promising platform for future laboratory WEP tests.

papers.title: Kernel Ridge Attention: Nonlinear Memory with Selective Forgetting
papers.abstract: Kernel Ridge Attention (KRA) is a recurrent sequence mixer that combines learned nonlinear features with covariance-guided memory updates. It stores associations through recursive ridge regression, using correlations among past keys to determine how new observations modify memory. A content-dependent Ornstein--Uhlenbeck transition controls retention and restores uncertainty for future writes. This construction admits an exact temporal-kernel interpretation and maintains an inference state whose size is independent of context length. Associative block maps and explicit adjoints support parallel training while preserving the recursive update. In controlled language-modeling experiments, KRA improves prediction quality over attention and recurrent baselines, strengthens natural associative recall over the evaluated recurrent models, and achieves practical distributed training throughput. These properties provide a principled foundation for nonlinear, adaptive sequence memory.

papers.title: DIVO: a direct divertor configuration plasma start-up scheme aimed at tokamak fusion reactors
papers.abstract: The tokamak, one of the mainstream approaches to magnetic confinement in nuclear fusion devices, will be the first approach to reach reactor class prototyping. Plasma start-up is expected to be more challenging in large superconducting next-step tokamaks such as ITER due to the low inductive toroidal electric field and potentially long durations in limiter configuration when plasma-wall interactions lead to easier impurity contamination of the confined plasma. Such limiter start-up is the standard way of early plasma formation in the vast majority of today's experimental devices and is planned on ITER. To mitigate these issues, a novel plasma start-up scheme with divertor geometry only (DIVO start-up) was recently developed for the first time on the EAST superconducting tokamak. The key breakthrough in this work is the use of a non-inductive, electron cyclotron wave generated plasma formed in a poloidal field configuration which is a superposition of a barrel-like geometry around the centre of the vacuum vessel and a mirror-like geometry across the whole vessel cross-section. Such a non-inductive discharge avoids the drawback of low inductive electric field which is unavoidable in large superconducting devices as a consequence of the relatively low voltages which can be applied to the magnet coils. In addition to the low toroidal electric field, the DIVO start-up scheme as demonstrated on EAST significantly reduces impurity sources compared to the conventional limiter phase approach, even in cases with relatively poorly conditioned plasma-facing surfaces. The robustness of the DIVO start-up has also been verified on EAST with varying prefill gas pressure, impurity level and inductive electric field. It thus offers a potential solution to one of the main issues facing routine successful start-up on large tokamak reactors.

papers.title: Navigating Robots from Unknown and Uncalibrated Exocentric Cameras via Map Estimation
papers.abstract: Exocentric cameras, mounted on walls or ceilings in indoor environments, offer wider vantage points and are less easily occluded than robot-mounted cameras, making them an appealing alternative for perception in robot navigation algorithms. Previous methods that use such cameras, however, require their pose and intrinsics to be known before deployment, demanding calibration that is time-consuming, requires specialized personnel, and must be repeated whenever a camera moves or a new room is navigated. We propose Robot-centric Obstacle Maps from Unknown and uncalibrated eXocentric cameras (ROMUX), an agent that navigates a robot toward point goals while avoiding obstacles using exocentric cameras that are both uncalibrated, meaning the system does not require their pose or intrinsic information as input, and unknown, meaning it is not fit to a specific camera during training and does not require pre-deployment fine-tuning. We train a cross-view transformer on large-scale simulation data to predict metric robot-centric obstacle maps from exocentric images, without conditioning image tokens on camera information. A small policy trained with Proximal Policy Optimization (PPO) then navigates on the predicted maps toward a goal coordinate relative to the robot. We benchmark our agent in simulation with cameras randomized per episode, and it matches the success rates of a PPO policy that navigates from a robot-mounted camera. Further, ROMUX works with one camera or multiple cameras with partial views and has been transferred zero-shot to a real robot using a camera at varying positions and orientations across various room layouts.

papers.title: Asymptotic error of the accelerated exponential Euler scheme for semilinear parabolic SPDEs driven by fractional Brownian motion
papers.abstract: We study the strong convergence and asymptotic error of the accelerated exponential Euler scheme for semilinear parabolic stochastic partial differential equations driven by additive cylindrical fractional Brownian motion with Hurst parameter $H\in(\frac12,1)$. The drift is globally Lipschitz and Gâteaux differentiable, with a second directional derivative taking values in a negative-order space. Under a weighted Hilbert--Schmidt condition on the noise and suitable derivative bounds, we establish strong error estimates that reflect the interaction between noise regularity and drift regularity. In a regime where the strong order is one, the normalized error $m(X^m-X)$ converges in probability in $C([0,T];\V)$ to the unique continuous solution of a random linear integral equation. Its stochastic forcing is a divergence integral plus an explicit covariance correction. The proof combines a Gâteaux chain rule for Malliavin derivatives, uniform spectral approximations, and time increment estimates. Localization gives the result for independent random initial values with finite moments, together with lower-moment convergence at each fixed time.

papers.title: Vague rotational symmetry at BCC [100] twist grain boundaries
papers.abstract: In earlier work (arXiv:2603.21158) we introduced vague rotational symmetry for proximal coincidence point sets at grain boundaries. A prescribed rotation must be realizable at every pair tolerance $\varepsilon$ by moving each midpoint of an admitted atomic pair by at most $\varepsilon/2$, half the maximum pair separation. We prove the proposed classification for the planar model of a body-centred cubic $[100]$ twist boundary. On $0\leqθ\leq45^\circ$, the maximal rotational order is twelve at $30^\circ$, eight at $45^\circ$, and four at every other misorientation. Vague $n$-fold symmetry forces $ξ_n M=M$ for the Fourier module $M$, hence $\mathbb{Z}[ξ_n]\subseteq M$ in crystal coordinates. For every rotation of finite order preserving $M$, we determine the least uniform displacement for all sufficiently small $\varepsilon$, allowing independent point motions and a free rotation centre. In this regime twelvefold symmetry at $30^\circ$ costs $\varepsilon/(2\sqrt3)$, and eightfold symmetry at $45^\circ$ costs zero. At a twist of approximately $25.53^\circ$, the Fourier module also has eightfold symmetry, but realizing it in the plane costs $\sqrt2\,\varepsilon$.

papers.title: SixthView: A Benchmark for Hidden-View Reconstruction and 3D Assembly Reasoning
papers.abstract: Inferring the unseen side of a 3D assembly requires reasoning about part placement and occlusion. Different assemblies can match the observed views while producing different hidden views, leaving the target ambiguous. We introduce SixthView, a benchmark in which models predict a sixth orthographic view from five observed views and information about the component shapes. The benchmark contains 602 synthetic polycube assemblies with 2--10 parts and requires a dense grid of part labels for the missing view, allowing both exact-view and cell-level evaluation. For each item, we exhaustively verify that all legal assemblies consistent with the exact component geometry and observed label grids yield the same target view. With these inputs, the task tests symbolic assembly and coordinate reasoning. The image-only variants additionally require shape recovery from rendered views, where occlusion can make different 3D shapes look identical. We evaluate three vision-language models under four input conditions. Across 552 items with complete evaluations, exact-grid accuracy with images plus exact text ranges from 33.2% to 85.4%. Adding exact text to separate images improves accuracy by 19.7--63.0 percentage points, whereas adding images to exact text changes it by only $-0.5$ to $+2.1$ points. Separate image panels outperform a merged sheet by 6.7--11.1 points. The results show that performance depends strongly on access to exact symbolic information, with little further improvement from images once the geometry is specified. GitHub: https://github.com/facebookresearch/sixthview_benchmark

papers.title: EVA-RSI: Recursive Self-Improvement of Video Evaluators for Judging Temporal Quality
papers.abstract: Video evaluators play an important role in video generation, yet they miss motion defects, limiting the quality of generated videos. Recursive self-improvement (RSI) has made strong progress in mathematics and coding, where explicit verifiers provide reliable feedback on a single goal. Video evaluation poses two difficulties for RSI: it has no verifier, and it must judge many dimensions at once, such as physics, smoothness and dynamics, where a gain on one can cost another. We introduce EVA-RSI, a multi-agent framework for exploring RSI under these two constraints. We build a fixed proxy exam with construction-defined targets by applying controlled changes to videos, such as temporal reversal and frame dropping. These edits supply supervision without human annotation. A small set of human-labeled real videos anchors the exam to human judgment. Each dimension has an LLM agent that proposes improvements. A leader agent coordinates the proposals, and a Nash bargaining rule selects updates that balance progress across dimensions. Humans design the exam, review candidate changes and revise the curriculum between stages. Starting from Qwen3-VL-8B, EVA-RSI improves motion evaluation, with the largest gain on smoothness, and the gains carry over to defect types never seen during the run. On the dynamics subsets of public benchmarks, our evaluator achieves the highest observed scores among 21 tested models. As an RL reward, it increases generated motion and earns human preference. A data-selection pipeline incorporating it also increases motion.

papers.title: Beyond Additive Composition: Interventional Modeling of State-Dependent Cross-Degradation Responses for Composite Image Restoration
papers.abstract: Composite image restoration aims to recover images corrupted by multiple coexisting degradations. Existing methods predominantly decompose composite corruptions into individual factors, relying on these isolated priors to guide restoration. However, coexisting degradations are inherently interdependent: the manifestation of one degradation dynamically shifts with the states of others, inducing non-additive interactions that factor-wise paradigms fail to capture. To bridge this gap, we formulate state-dependent cross-degradation responses and propose PROBE, an interventional framework that explicitly models how coexisting degradations influence one another. Specifically, we first construct unified degradation axes by aligning visual and textual degraded-clean offsets. Along these axes, a calibrated coordinate head estimates current degradation states, while bidirectional feature perturbations are injected to probe cross-coordinate responses under the current states. Contrasting these responses with corresponding intensity-matched single-degradation references quantifies intrinsic non-additive deviations, allowing the resulting response descriptors and state coordinates to jointly guide restoration. For comprehensive evaluation, we introduce SCD-15, a new benchmark covering all 15 nonempty combinations of four degradation factors at three severity levels. Experiments demonstrate that PROBE achieves state-of-the-art performance on the CDD-11, AWMM-100K, and SCD-15 composite restoration datasets using a compact model with modest GPU memory requirements.

papers.title: Imaging chiral snake states in a qubit array with programmable gauge fields
papers.abstract: Spatially varying magnetic fields steer charged particles along directed paths. Where a field reverses sign, particles follow snake-like orbits along the reversal line, in a direction set by both the field orientation and the sign of their energy. Transport measurements have detected such snake states, but imaging their dynamics in a reprogrammable field landscape remains challenging. Here we digitally simulate the Harper--Hofstadter model with programmable synthetic magnetic fields on a 49-qubit superconducting processor. In each Trotter step, every hopping term is one native fractional-iSWAP gate, and single-qubit $Z$ rotations set all 36 plaquette fluxes independently, without additional entangling gates. Uniform, random, and stepped flux landscapes reveal Aharonov--Bohm suppression of diagonal propagation, disorder-induced slowing, and magnetic reflection. At a field reversal, bonding and antibonding initial states, which carry opposite energy biases, propagate in opposite directions, and both directions reverse when the field is inverted. A symmetry analysis of these reversals yields a chiral displacement of nearly one lattice spacing after ten Trotter rounds, with symmetry-breaking residuals below 0.05 lattice spacings. Bond-resolved flux programming with site-resolved imaging thus provides a quantitative tool for synthetic gauge fields and a route to time-dependent gauge fields and interacting particles.

papers.title: Can AI Understand Indonesian Children's Book Illustrations? Compliance, Safety, and the Cultural Alignment Gap
papers.abstract: Children's book illustrations carry developmental, pedagogical, and cultural responsibilities that are often formally codified in guidelines. As AI systems begin entering children's publishing pipelines, both as evaluators and as generators, a natural question arises: can they reliably meet the structural, safety, and cultural standards required? We investigate this across three criteria: guideline compliance, safety, and cultural alignment, using Indonesia's Book Leveling Guideline as a government-issued evaluation framework with explicit visual criteria for four reading levels. To understand how well VLMs can identify and apply these guideline criteria, we first evaluate them on real published children's book pages and compare their assessments against a human baseline. To then examine whether AI-generated illustrations meet the same standards, we apply the VLM judge to images produced by two generation models and cross-check them against a subset of human illustrator raters. We find that VLMs are reliable on explicit criteria such as compliance and safety, but fall short on cultural alignment, systematically missing content that human raters flag as culturally inappropriate. AI-generated illustrations show the same blind spot: they satisfy structural and safety criteria but fail to capture implicit cultural details that human raters consistently identify.

papers.title: Risk-Controlled Correction for Frozen Multimodal Models under Missing Modalities
papers.abstract: A deployed multimodal predictor may face missing modalities after its weights can no longer be changed. This raises a question that training-time repair does not answer: what part of the resulting error is still correctable from the information that remains? We show that this part is characterized by the Bayes gap, the difference between the model's prediction and the Bayes prediction given the observed modalities. For cross-entropy and squared error, excess risk measures this gap in the geometry of the loss; ambiguity in the observed modalities cannot be removed. Thus, a badly degraded prediction is not necessarily a correctable one. Estimating the Bayes prediction normally requires labels. However, when a model observing more modalities is conditionally correct, averaging its outputs conditional on the remaining modalities recovers this target without retrieval labels; with the same fixed blend and neighbors, it is no worse in expected cross-entropy or Brier risk than averaging hard labels. Some such assumption is unavoidable: otherwise the target is not identifiable from unlabeled data alone. GUARD (Gated Utility-Aware Recalibration for Deployment) leaves the deployed predictor unchanged. It estimates a candidate correction by retrieval, learns from deployment-matched labeled data when correction is likely to help, and calibrates a threshold on a held-out split by conformal risk control. Under exchangeability, the marginal probability that GUARD applies a correction whose loss increase exceeds a prescribed tolerance is bounded by a preset level, regardless of the learned score. In controlled experiments, correction gain follows headroom rather than raw error; across nine frozen model-dataset pairs spanning six domains, GUARD retains most of blanket correction's gain within harm budgets that blanket correction often exceeds.

papers.title: Quasi-Bisections of Cubic Graphs with Tree and Circuit Decompositions
papers.abstract: A $2$-quasi-bisection of a graph is a vertex $2$-coloring in which the color classes differ in size by at most two and every monochromatic component has at most two vertices. Esperet, Mazzuoccolo, and Tarsi in [J. Graph Theory, 86(2017), 149-158] conjectured that every cubic graph admits such a coloring. DeVos and Nurse proved the conjecture for cubic graphs whose edge sets can be partitioned into a tree and a circuit. This result is generalized in this paper for a larger family of cubic graphs. The conjecture is verified for cubic graphs whose edge set can be partitioned into two subsets $E(T)$ and $E(J)$, where $T$ is a tree of $G$ and $J$ is an even subgraph containing at most two odd circuit components.

papers.title: Long-lived linear slow roll near critical and spinodal points in soft-wall AdS/QCD
papers.abstract: We systematically investigate the real-time evolution of the chiral condensate near critical and spinodal points within soft-wall AdS/QCD, focusing primarily on the long-lived prethermalization stage, in contrast to the conventional early transients and late-time relaxation. While the quasi-steady nature of this stage has been previously identified, we demonstrate that it is intrinsically a continuous linear slow roll, fundamentally distinct from the asymptotic critical slowing down at late times. By showing that the bulk evolution adiabatically follows the boundary condensate on a slow configuration space, we analytically project the 5D partial differential equation onto a boundary first-order Ginzburg-Landau (GL) equation. We find that the long lifetime of this linear regime is protected by a ``double-zero'' condition: the simultaneous vanishing of the local potential gradient (suppressing the drift velocity) and curvature (suppressing the acceleration). This geometric flatness inherently emerges at the second-order point and both first-order spinodal endpoints. Crucially, this behavior is not a fine-tuned artifact, but a generic consequence of the effective potential landscape intrinsic to these phase-transition endpoints, persisting across a broad class of physically relevant initial conditions and temperature quenches. A local short-time expansion further relates the interval duration to the potential curvature and its higher-order derivatives, in good agreement with our numerical simulations. This work establishes a direct link between the local structure of phase-transition endpoints and the dynamical evolution of the long-lived intermediate stage of the condensate.

papers.title: Accelerating Distributed Digital Ising Machines
papers.abstract: Ising machines, dedicated accelerators built around the dynamics of Ising-like spin models, have emerged as a leading platform for combinatorial optimization and probabilistic sampling. The problems that motivate them require millions of spins, far beyond the on-chip capacity of any single device, so a practical Ising machine must distribute its computation across many devices. Prior work reports throughput at a single operating point, leaving the binding resource unidentified and platform crossovers measurable only by experiment; no calibrated cross-platform cost model of distributed Ising machines has been reported, nor have systematic techniques to accelerate their Markov chain Monte Carlo (MCMC) workloads. This work presents a calibrated cost model that decomposes digital Ising sweep time into compute, memory, synchronization, and inter-device communication terms, validated with 4.8% mean error across three GPU generations, FPGA and ASIC up to 1 million spins. Guided by the model, we address each term in turn and propose: (i) a data placement strategy, worth up to 4.2$\times$ speedup; (ii) multi-rate and bounded-staleness schedules that relax the barrier that Gibbs sampling imposes, cutting time-to-solution (TTS) by up to 3.16$\times$ on three benchmarks; and (iii) a phase-offset streaming dataflow that hides boundary exchange behind interior computation whenever a link satisfies a latency-transparency criterion, yielding up to 1.25$\times$/1.74$\times$/2.01$\times$ on an H200 pair, a ZCU106 pair, and a four-board XEM8320 $2{\times}2$ mesh. The streaming dataflow is also implemented on a fabricated four-chip 28 nm ASIC sustaining 28.1 Gflips/s at 4.81 pJ/flip.

papers.title: Local spin constraints and symmetry in single-$Q$ spiral magnets
papers.abstract: The Luttinger--Tisza (LT) method provides a lower bound on the energy of classical spin models but relaxes the local spin-length constraints. For a generic incommensurate single-$Q$ spiral, fixed spin length requires circular polarization on every magnetic sublattice, a condition not guaranteed by equal sublattice weights in the lowest LT eigenmode. We develop a constrained formulation for general bilinear classical spin Hamiltonians with one or two magnetic sublattices. For one sublattice, minimization reduces to a secular equation for the spiral-plane normal. For two sublattices, exact elimination of the relative phase gives a frame-independent energy on the space of two unit normals. We derive symmetry constraints by distinguishing operations that preserve or reverse the Fourier arm and those that preserve or exchange sublattices. For a model with symmetric anisotropy, numerical optimization over both spiral-plane normals yields a lower energy than either constrained pure exchange-sector state, despite the block diagonalization of the linear Hamiltonian. A separate anisotropic two-sublattice benchmark demonstrates that enforcing local circularity can shift the preferred ordering wave vector even when the lowest LT eigenmode has equal sublattice weights.

papers.title: NullTok: empirical-null token selection for training-free long video understanding
papers.abstract: Long video understanding remains a daunting challenge for existing multimodal large language models (MLLMs), mainly due to the large number of visual tokens accumulated in long videos. Currently, frame selection and token selection are two main paradigms for addressing this issue, both aiming to select relevant visual information to form a compact input for MLLMs. A natural approach combines these two paradigms by selecting frames before pruning tokens, but noisy frame-level relevance estimates can cause irreversible evidence loss. In this paper, we study this problem from the perspective of assessing the spatiotemporal distribution of query-specific evidence and propose a novel and training-free approach termed NULLTOK. For every patch across all frames, we construct an empirical-null distribution from 64 group-matched irrelevant control queries, capturing the scores expected in the absence of target-specific evidence. Target affinities are calibrated against these same-position references into right-tail Monte Carlo p-values, which are discrete super-uniform under a conditional exchangeability assumption. Calibrated screening and a high-recall semantic guard produce candidate tokens for deterministic visual deduplication and joint spatiotemporal budget allocation. To validate NullTok, we apply it to two representative MLLMs and conduct extensive experiments on a set of video benchmarks. The experimental results demonstrate its effectiveness under a bounded visual token budget. For example, it achieves 65.81% and 68.85% on Video-MME using frozen LLaVA-Video-7B and Qwen3-VL-8B backbones, respectively, at a cap of 64 full-frame equivalents (FFE), without subtitles or audio. These results outperform all evaluated baselines on Video-MME under the same budget for both backbones. Code is available at https://github.com/potato-kitty/NullTok.

papers.title: A Rank-One Bypass of Fixed Linear Erasure
papers.abstract: Linear concept erasure can make a target unreadable to a specified family of linear classifiers applied to a model's current internal features. In an open-weight release, however, an attacker can modify the layers that produce those features. We study a fixed affine erasure layer whose upstream model is allowed to change. If the layer transmits even one direction visible to an allowed downstream classifier, the attacker can write a target score into that direction and carry it through the layer. We show that this condition is also necessary, and that for a nonconstant linear target score the required change is a rank-one affine update. Across six CIFAR-10 class-pair tasks, the route restores nearly all pre-erasure target performance and can leave a deployed benign linear head's scores unchanged to numerical tolerance. We then price the attack: with eight target labels and 2,000 unlabelled calibration examples, a 10% mean relative feature edit yields 79.8% test accuracy, which is 91.2% of the fitted score's gain over chance; tighter edit limits sharply reduce success. Linear guardedness therefore remains a valid guarantee about the current representation, but it is not by itself a tamper-resistance guarantee for an editable open-weight model.

papers.title: Locality-Aware Scheduling for Stream Processing Applications in Serverless Environments
papers.abstract: Stateful Serverless (Function-as-a-Service) environment are increasingly used for stream processing applications. These applications are often structured as pipelines where data flows through a sequence of distinct processing operators. Many operators are stateful and require access to the processing state during execution. To address this, stateful serverless platforms introduce state servers on worker nodes, co-locating state with computation to dramatically reduce access latency. In serverless, these data pipelines are realized by chaining function invocations, passing the processed data from one function to the next. To reduce network overhead, state-of-the-art scheduling approaches employ a distributed worker-level scheduling model, routing locally generated chained requests directly to destination workers, bypassing centralized schedulers. However, these approaches always co-locate state and execution for the same operator in the same worker, which forces most invocations to the next operator to be transferred across workers, thereby increasing both latency and I/O overhead. As a result, this paper proposes LcSched, a novel distributed scheduling strategy tailored for stream processing applications in stateful serverless environments. LcSched seeks to maximise local execution of chained function invocations while ensuring that each execution accesses its state from the local worker. It also monitors workload at runtime to maintain workload balance between workers. Experimental results show that LcSched improves throughput by up to 3.6x and reduces end-to-end latency by up to 79% compared to the state-of-the-art distributed scheduling strategy for stateful serverless environments.

papers.title: Infinity-Wasserstein Distributionally Robust Principal Component Analysis: Exact Reformulation, Finite-Sample Guarantee, and Efficient Algorithm
papers.abstract: Principal component analysis (PCA) is a fundamental and ubiquitous technique for dimension reduction and representation learning, yet its empirical formulation remains vulnerable to distributional uncertainty. While distributionally robust optimization (DRO) offers a natural remedy, existing order-2 Wasserstein models of PCA either preserve the nominal PCA subspace or lack an exact reformulation. This paper demonstrates how the infinity-Wasserstein distance can reconcile these two desirable properties. For the resulting DRO model of PCA, we derive an exact finite-dimensional reformulation and explicitly identify a worst-case distribution attaining the inner maximum. Crucially, the reformulated objective retains samplewise residual information beyond the empirical covariance matrix, revealing a mechanism through which distributional robustness can reshape the learned principal subspace. Under the mild assumption that the true distribution has a finite fourth moment, we further establish a uniform finite-sample performance guarantee for the proposed model. An iteratively reweighted majorization-minimization algorithm is also developed to solve the resulting nonconvex and nonsmooth optimization problem, with a rigorous analysis of its convergence properties. Numerical experiments substantiate the computational efficiency of the proposed algorithm and the practical effectiveness of the infinity-Wasserstein model in downstream applications.

papers.title: SWE-growth: Teacher-Guided Adaptive Self-Play for Software Engineering Agents
papers.abstract: Self-play offers a scalable way to train software engineering agents by generating repository-level repair tasks. However, with binary repair rewards and finite rollout budgets, all-fail groups provide no reward-based group-relative advantage. Such tasks may still offer learning opportunities when a Teacher can provide verified repairs absent from the Student's own attempts. We introduce SWE-Growth, a teacher-guided adaptive self-play framework that uses verified Teacher outcomes to identify learning opportunities for the current Student. Tasks with all students failure but reliable Teacher success provide demonstrations for supervised fine-tuning (SFT), and post-SFT Student rollouts identify mixed-outcome tasks with a positive Teacher--Student gap for reinforcement learning. Task eligibility also guides Injector updates, connecting Student training with subsequent task generation. Starting from 101 seed issues, \textsc{SWE-Growth} improves Qwen3-Coder-30B-A3B-Instruct from 27.7% to 31.7% on SWE-bench Pro and from 11.0% to 17.2% on held-out TerminalBench 2.1 by Round~2. It exceeds Student-only self-play by 2.6 and 4.1 percentage points, respectively, and Teacher-augmented self-play by 1.8 and 2.5 points under approximately matched budgets. These results support adapting both supervision and task selection to the Student's evolving repair capability.

papers.title: In Situ Training of Optical Neural Networks by Coding Agents
papers.abstract: Optical neural networks promise fast, energy-efficient computing, but every device departs from its design and must be trained with the hardware. In situ training relies on an expert-built calibrated digital model of each device or on gradient-free trial and error. Coding agents, large language models that write and run programs, have shown an emergent ability to understand and edit the weights of digital neural networks. Here we introduce optics as code, a method in which a coding agent trains an optical neural network from measurements alone, through a harness that returns camera images of its probes and requires a hypothesis per request. We discovered that the agent forms a physical understanding of the optics and reparametrizes the network with interpretable optical elements tuned on the hardware. It outperforms gradient-free methods in classification and image encoding, approaching backpropagation through a calibrated model at a fraction of the cost. Needing neither per-device calibration nor gradients through the hardware, and improving with more capable models, optics as code offers a practical route to large, scalable optical neural networks and a general tool for calibrating and optimizing optical experiments.

papers.title: Indecomposable representations of $C^{\infty}(S^1,\aff)$ on polynomial spaces over jet spaces
papers.abstract: We study a class of finite dimensional complex vector spaces \(\pn\), \(n \in \bn\), consisting of polynomials on \(\jnmc\), the space of \((n-1)\) jets at a fixed point \(t_0 \in S^1\) of \(C^\infty\) functions \(S^1 \to \bc\). The loop group \(C^\infty(S^1,\aff)\) of the affine group \(\aff\) acts naturally on \(\pn\) by an indecomposable linear representation. The space \(\pn\) is canonically isomorphic to the space of holomorphic sections of a certain line bundle over the loop space of the Riemann sphere. It has an intricate structure, leading to infinite families of combinatorial identities. In this paper, we establish necessary conditions for a polynomial on \(\jnmc\) to belong to \(\pn\). Furthermore, we give partial answers to several conjectures concerning \(\pn\).

papers.title: Technical Note on Matlantis PFP v9: Extending the Element and Domain Coverage of the r2SCAN Training Data
papers.abstract: Universal machine learning interatomic potentials (uMLIPs) make atomistic simulations possible at scales beyond the reach of density functional theory (DFT). Matlantis PFP is a uMLIP that treats a variety of domains, including crystals, molecules, and surfaces, with a single model. PFP v8 incorporated a training dataset computed with the r2SCAN functional, chosen for its good agreement with experiment, but the elements and domains covered by that dataset were limited. Here we present Matlantis PFP v9, in which the training data computed with the r2SCAN functional are extended to the lanthanides from Pr to Lu and to the elements from Po to Cm, for a total of 96 elements, and to additional domains such as clusters and adsorption structures. The formation energies of crystals containing the newly supported elements reproduce experimental standard enthalpies of formation with the same level of accuracy as crystals composed only of previously supported elements, and the adsorption energies of molecules on transition-metal surfaces have an overall error against experiment comparable to that of DFT-PBE, although chemisorbed species are overbound. On the same type of GPU (A100), the inference speed and the maximum system size exceed those of SevenNet-Omni, a public uMLIP trained on r2SCAN data: forces are evaluated three to four times faster, and five to ten times as many atoms can be handled. As a result, PFP-R2SCAN is now applicable to systems containing rare-earth and actinide elements and to adsorption on surfaces.

papers.title: Keep the Image in Mind: A Visual Board for Multimodal Agents
papers.abstract: Multi-step visual reasoning suffers when early visual misinterpretations persist as incorrect premises in subsequent reasoning. We argue that how visual evidence is represented during reasoning matters as much as how much of it is gathered. Rather than appending observations and inferences to an ever-growing dialogue, we introduce a Visual Board-centered harness that separates visual observations, uncertain interpretations, and derived reasoning within a structured, capacity-bounded, and revisable workspace. This separation makes each premise explicit and auditable, so that conflicts between what is seen and what is derived become detectable even by a text-only critic and can trigger targeted reinspection of the original image. Without task-specific training, our harness consistently outperforms standalone models across 4B, 8B, Qwen3-VL-Flash, and 32B configurations on Euclid30K, SolidGeo, and ChartQA bar charts, with gains of up to 11.68, 18.42, and 24.82 percentage points, respectively. Under identical tools, critic, and interaction limits, the structured Board outperforms shared free-form notes by 6.67 to 13.00 points and no-Board retries by 7.35 to 18.80 points while using 7.9\% to 38.2\% fewer tokens. Supervised fine-tuning on harness trajectories further improves direct answering and critic-free tool use, with positive transfer to chart reasoning.

papers.title: HOForce: Motion and Force Reconstruction of Hand-Object Interaction Using a Single-View RGB-D Video
papers.abstract: Reconstructing hand-object interactions is an important task, and achieving it with a single camera makes large-scale capture practical but challenging due to heavy occlusions. We introduce HOForce to track hands and objects, and further recover interaction forces from single-view RGB-D video and known object properties. For two-hand manipulation, we jointly model fingertip forces of both hands and the contact forces between objects when two objects are presented. The reconstructed forces also improve motion tracking by giving pose constraints in the occluded regions. HOForce recovers hand and object motion more accurately on DexYCB and TACO and produces less hand-object penetration than interaction baselines on DexYCB. On our dataset of fingertip forces recorded with tactile sensors, HOForce reduces normal-force MAE by 24.5% relative to the strongest baseline. The recovered forces reproduce object motion in MuJoCo and transfer to other engines after adaptation.

papers.title: Localized active phase in the coevolving voter model with fixed links
papers.abstract: The coevolving voter model (CVM) describes the evolution of node states and network topology through copying and rewiring dynamics. It traditionally assumes that all ties can be rewired, overlooking unbreakable real-world relationships like family or close friendships. To address this, we introduce fixed links that cannot be rewired and study how these structural constraints modify the collective dynamics of the CVM. In addition to the active and frozen phases of the CVM, we find a new localized active phase in which activity is sustained, beyond a percolation transition, by a giant component of fixed links. The existence of this new phase is predicted by a moment-closure approximation that goes beyond the standard pair approximation. The finite-size manifestation of this phase is an asymmetric fragmented phase. In addition, the active-frozen transition of the CVM, manifested as a fragmentation transition for finite systems, is delayed by the existence of fixed links to larger values of the rewiring rate.

papers.title: Coupled-channel pole structure and bare-state mixing of bottom-strange heavy-quark spin partners
papers.abstract: Motivated by the observation of the $B_{s0}^*(5700)$ and the heavy-quark symmetry relations connecting the $DK$, $D^*K$, $\bar{B}K$, and $\bar B^*K$ systems, we investigate whether the same chiral dynamics can generate negative-parity partners dominated by the $\bar B_1K$ and $\bar B_2^*K$ components. We further examine how nearby bare bottom-strange states reshape the pole spectrum through coupled-channel mixing. Both the relevant $S$-wave scattering and the lower-lying $P$-wave decay channels are explicitly included in the coupled-channel calculation. In the absence of bare states, the interaction generates two negative-parity poles near $6.15$ GeV. Coupling the hadronic channels to the corresponding quark-model configurations leads to a richer two-pole structure in each sector, with the pole masses, widths, and channel residues governed by the interplay between the bare states and the hadronic dynamics. In particular, the inclusion of the bare states substantially increases the widths of the negative-parity poles with the larger $S$-wave molecular components. The resulting correlated patterns in the pole spectrum provide testable signatures for future studies of excited bottom-strange mesons.

papers.title: Generalizing the Gaster--Loustau Theorem via Generalized Discrete Markov Spectra
papers.abstract: We realize generalized Markov numbers (GM numbers) for arbitrary $k_1,k_2,k_3\in \mathbb Z_{\ge0}$ as $λ$-lengths of return arcs on a hyperbolic orbifold constructed from local monodromy matrices. The McShane identity of Tan--Wong--Zhang on this orbifold yields a summation identity with multiplicities for the gaps between the associated Markov--Lagrange constants and their limiting value, together with a summation inequality that counts each distinct value once. These results extend the summation identity and inequality of Gaster and Loustau to generalized Markov numbers.

papers.title: Control-Aware Separating Hyperplanes for Control Barrier Functions in Planar Navigation
papers.abstract: Separating hyperplanes are widely used in Control Barrier Function (CBF)-based collision avoidance, yet their orientations strongly govern control intervention-the deviation of the applied control from the robot's nominal command. Existing methods typically select hyperplane orientations from geometry alone. Jointly optimizing orientations and control yields a continuous, non-convex problem in which local nonlinear solvers suffer from initialization sensitivity, local minima, and unpredictable latency, while discretized orientation grids scale exponentially with obstacle count. For planar navigation of a polygonal robot among polygonal obstacles, we present a solver-free, control-aware separating hyperplane selection method that directly computes a global optimum of this joint problem at each step whenever it is feasible. Exploiting the geometry of Minkowski difference polygons, we reduce this continuous non-convex optimization to evaluating a polynomial-size set of candidate control interventions via closed-form algebraic checks, selecting the feasible candidate of minimum norm. Across 250 simulated navigation scenarios, our method reduces cumulative intervention cost by 3.6% at the median and 27.3% at the 90th percentile compared to a local nonlinear solver, and completion time by 0.6% and 5.6%, respectively. In scalability benchmarks, it achieves a 6.1x per-step speedup at 16 simultaneous obstacles.

papers.title: Tuning spreading transport in GaN HEMTs with an AlN space layer under non-equilibrium heating
papers.abstract: Lateral spreading transport dominates near-junction heat dissipation in GaN high-electron-mobility transistors, yet thermal control has largely overlooked this geometry. It neither reaches the core AlGaN/GaN region nor, beyond the spatial spreading itself, accounts for the spectral non-equilibrium of the heat source. Here we tune the spreading resistance directly by inserting a thin, highly conducting AlN space layer above the source to intercept heat and divert it laterally. We test this approach across GaN, AlGaN/GaN, and AlGaN/AlN/GaN structures under both equilibrium and longitudinal-optical (LO)-pumped non-equilibrium heating, pairing non-equilibrium molecular dynamics (NEMD) with full-band phonon Monte Carlo (MC). In equilibrium, the AlN layer lowers the spreading resistance by 38% relative to the AlGaN-capped structure and by 17% relative to bare GaN, with little change in the one-dimensional resistance. The equilibrium color map over AlN thickness and interfacial bonding shows a strong interface effect but a weak thickness trend that reverses, so the gain is set by interface admission rather than solely by thickness or bulk conductivity. This ordering is independently confirmed by gray MC simulations. Under LO pumping, the spreading resistance rises by 58-83% in NEMD and by 9-20% in MC, and the equilibrium spatial optimum weakens or even reverses. This is because an optical-to-acoustic conversion gate now precedes every spatial gate and locks energy in slow optical modes. The three gates in series (optical-to-acoustic conversion, interface admission, and lateral diversion) close into a single non-equilibrium resistance network that predicts the full-band MC cases and frames the AlN space layer as a design variable within the non-equilibrium source state.

papers.title: On Demand, Not Uniformity: Adaptive Expert Orchestration for Multimodal Continual Instruction Tuning
papers.abstract: Multimodal Continual Instruction Tuning (MCIT) enables Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs) to adapt to sequential instruction data while retaining previously acquired knowledge. While recent Mixture-of-Experts (MoE)-based methods mitigate forgetting by freezing historical experts and introducing new ones, they largely overlook the varying adaptation demands across tasks. Probing incoming tasks reveals pronounced heterogeneity in layer-wise gradient pressure and token-wise prediction difficulty. This observation highlights two unresolved decisions: where additional capacity is needed and how strongly new experts should contribute to individual tokens. To address both questions, we propose the Coverage-Calibrated Expert Injection and Residual Arbitration framework (CIRA-MoE), which derives expert acceptance margins via learnable threshold routing to serve as a unified coverage signal. Specifically, historical acceptance evidence guides the selective injection of new experts into insufficiently covered layers. Meanwhile, relative evidence between historical and current experts modulates token-wise residual contributions, coupled with arbitration-consistent regularization to promote expert specialization. Comprehensive experiments on UCIT and CoIN demonstrate that CIRA-MoE outperforms existing state-of-the-art methods in MCIT.

papers.title: Asking but Missing: Decision Coverage in Natural-Language Data Querying
papers.abstract: Large language models are increasingly used to translate natural language questions about structured data into executable programs. A fundamental challenge is recognizing when a question admits multiple computational interpretations and identifying the decisions needed to resolve them. We investigate whether language models recognize these unresolved decisions before generating code, or silently adopt assumptions that may lead to incorrect results. We refer to the latter behavior as Underspecified Decision Completion (UDC). To distinguish different causes of UDC, we introduce Grounded Code Generation (GCG), a diagnostic protocol that separates the identification of unresolved decisions, their resolution using evidence, and their translation into executable code. By examining each stage separately, we can determine where the decisions responsible for incorrect results were first missed or mishandled. We evaluate this framework on BIRD-Pandas with twelve models. The results show that answering clarification questions consistently improves execution accuracy, yet substantial errors remain. Our findings suggest that the main difficulty lies not in answering clarification questions, but in recognizing which questions need to be asked in the first place.

papers.title: Comparing Data-Driven and Numerical Weather Prediction Forecasts of Extreme Weather: A Review
papers.abstract: Data-driven weather forecasting models, chiefly trained on reanalysis data, now match or beat physics-based numerical weather prediction (NWP) models on most headline scores, but whether this advantage extends to extreme weather is contested. We review peer-reviewed studies that directly compare data-driven forecasts with NWP for extremes, from nowcasting to subseasonal lead times. We discuss grey literature in the outlook but do not include it in the formal review. There is good agreement on the fact that data-driven models mostly outperform NWP on temperature extremes, tropical cyclone tracks and the location of synoptic features across time scales. The evidence is mixed for extreme precipitation and feature-based extreme event detection such as extremes related to atmospheric rivers, while it leans toward better NWP performance for estimating event intensity. For record-breaking events that lie outside the training distribution, the evidence is narrower. Nonetheless, both a systematic global evaluation and several case studies find that physics-based models retain the advantage, with data-driven models underestimating both the frequency and the magnitude of records. Hybrid systems that post-process NWP with machine-learning (ML), or couple data-driven forecasts with physics-based models, deliver some of the largest and most consistent gains. We argue that headline scores, verification choices and case selection explain much of the apparent disagreement in the literature, and provide recommendations for a more trustworthy and interpretable evaluation of data-driven models for extreme and record-breaking weather.

papers.title: Grounding Radiology Reports in 3D Chest CT: Results of the ReXGrounding Challenge
papers.abstract: Segmenting each reported finding in a radiology scan would allow findings to be measured and tracked over time and let AI systems generate reports that are verifiable, but so far AI models have performed poorly at this task. To advance this task, we organized the ReXGrounding Challenge at MICCAI 2026, the first challenge dedicated to it. Given a non-contrast chest CT scan and the set of findings from its report, participants trained models to produce the corresponding set of 3D segmentations. The challenge used 2,992 training and 200 validation scans from the ReXGroundingCT dataset, and evaluated methods on a held-out test set of 300 scans with 582 findings, exhaustively annotated by board-certified radiologists. In total, 48 teams from 15 countries made 760 submissions, and the best method reached a Dice of 0.375 and a hit rate of 0.77, matching agreement between two independent radiologist groups (Dice 0.32, hit rate 0.76, on a 50-scan subset). On the 100 scans of the pre-challenge benchmark, the winner reached a Dice of 0.390, against 0.285 for VoxTell, the best model before the challenge, which five of the six best teams fine-tuned. Non-focal findings remained far harder to segment than focal ones, instance F1 stayed below inter-reader agreement (0.34 vs. 0.47), and models sometimes segmented the right abnormality in the wrong location. Top methods thus match radiologist agreement in Dice, but non-focal findings, findings with multiple instances, and adherence to the anatomical location described in the text remain open problems.

papers.title: Aharonov-Bohm blockade of complete reversal in coupled Rabi cavities
papers.abstract: When a common bias reverses two bistable fields, the system can pass through either of two single-reversal configurations on its way to the favored state. We show that interference between these two orders of reversal can block the final step. In a dimer of coupled quantum Rabi cavities, the four field configurations form a loop, and a complex photon-hopping amplitude threads it with an Aharonov-Bohm flux. Near half a flux quantum, the two paths to complete reversal interfere destructively: in microscopic simulations, a slow uniform sweep reverses one field with probability 0.998, although the final bias favors reversing both. A four-state model calibrated at zero bias predicts how the window of this Aharonov-Bohm blockade narrows with sweep time. The blocked state remains coherent. A differential pulse followed by a return sweep converts the relative phase of the two single-reversal configurations into a fringe in the joint field signs, with contrast 0.95. In a trimer, a phase gradient imprinted between sweeps determines whether the next sweep adds or removes a reversed field: reversing the second of two gradients changes the most probable outcome from three reversed fields to one.

papers.title: MobileWeave: Program-First Synthesis of Dependency-Linked Tasks for Training Mobile GUI Agents
papers.abstract: Native mobile GUI agents require large-scale training trajectories covering both individual app functions and multi-goal workflows within and across apps, which makes automatic task synthesis a promising way to scale training data. Existing synthesis pipelines, however, produce each task as free-form text, leaving implicit how its subgoals depend on one another. This matters because composition is a skill in its own right: a policy may complete each subtask of a workflow on its own, yet fail to chain these subtasks into the complete workflow. We present MobileWeave, which instead synthesizes every task as an executable program derived from the app implementations of a controllable simulator. MobileWeave abstracts each app into a typed capability graph with semantic types shared across apps, composes atomic programs into single- and cross-app composite programs through explicit value and object dependencies, and verifies each program by native execution, deriving both its instruction and its completion check from the same program. Trained on teacher trajectories collected for these tasks and on recovery supervision at the policy's own stalls, MobileWeave-8B improves its base model by 26.7 points on MobileGym and by 8.6, 21.3, and 17.6 points on AndroidWorld, AndroidLab, and MobileWorld, with comparable gains at 4B. Beyond these gains, we find that composition is learnable from task structure: explicit dependencies between subgoals act as a training signal that teaches a policy to compose skills it already masters. We release data, model, and code at https://maxxnotmarx.github.io/MobileWeave/ .

papers.title: LAGR: Language-Aware Grasp Re-Ranking for Task Oriented Grasping
papers.abstract: Grasping is a fundamental capability for robotic manipulation, with the appropriate grasp depending on the downstream task. For example, a hammer should be held by its handle for hammering but by its head when it is handed over. Selecting such a grasp requires consideration of two criteria: physical feasibility on the object and suitability for the task. Developing such an approach requires dense grasp labels with both feasibility and task scores on real observations, but existing task-oriented grasping datasets are small, synthetic, or costly to annotate. To address this gap, we construct a dataset of 2.68 million scored 5-DoF grasp annotations over 100,911 image-task pairs from $17$ object categories. Additionally, we introduce LAGR, a task-oriented grasp detection method that explicitly addresses both these challenges. Given vision-language inputs, LAGR first generates task-independent grasp proposals along with a physical feasibility score, and then scores the generated grasps with a language-conditioned re-ranker that reasons over all proposals jointly. Experiments show that LAGR outperforms the next best method by 9.3 percentage points. We further validate LAGR on real objects by executing task-oriented grasps with a Franka Research 3 robot.

papers.title: Temporal Image Representations for Mouse Dynamics Authentication
papers.abstract: Mouse dynamics authentication has traditionally relied on handcrafted features or time-series representations that capture both spatial and temporal characteristics of mouse movements. More recent approaches have modeled mouse data as images, enabling the use of powerful pretrained computer vision models. However, prior work primarily focuses on spatial-only representations where the cursor coordinates are plotted as a trajectory image. These representations discard the temporal characteristics which can help discriminate users. In this work, we propose image representations that incorporate speed and velocity information for mouse dynamics authentication. We investigate two mouse data representations, a XYPlot representation that intuitively shows the path of movement, and a Pairwise Distance (PWD) representation that utilizes the entire image canvas to encode relationships between mouse events. Both representations are evaluated under both location-aware and location-free settings using pretrained 2D-CNN and ViT architectures. We found that the incorporation of temporal information improved performance over spatial representations alone, and that the location-aware variants generally outperformed the location-free. We achieve state-of-the-art performance on two datasets, Balabit and TWOS, and extend our evaluation to two other datasets. We found that in general, location-aware PWD with temporal encoding combined with the 2D-CNN architecture provided the best results, with mean EERs of 5.21% and 12.70% on the Balabit Test-1 and Test-2 sets, respectively, 4.94% on TWOS, 6.16% on ChaoShen, and 0.59% on DFL.

papers.title: Neural Memory Orchestration
papers.abstract: Modern HPC workloads increasingly stall on the memory hierarchy rather than on compute, and page faults from mmap'd files, swap, and tiered memory are a growing fraction of wall time. Heuristic prefetchers in the kernel handle stride-like and temporally clustered patterns well but degrade sharply on the irregular, data-dependent access streams typical of these workloads. Learned prefetchers have been shown to capture such patterns in simulation but have not been taken to a deployed pipeline running against live workloads on real hardware. We present Overseer, an end-to-end learned page-prefetching system. An eBPF collector observes page faults on the target host, a transformer predictor (OverNet) runs on network-attached inference hardware and emits future page addresses, and a kernel-resident enforcer materializes those pages into the target's address space before they are demanded. OverNet encodes fault sequences through per-instance ordinal ranks over deltas, which lets a single trained model serve any target process without retraining. On two page-fault-heavy workloads, Overseer reduces runtime by roughly 35% on Hilbert-curve traversal and by roughly an order of magnitude on dense matrix multiplication, with corresponding reductions in major-fault counts.

papers.title: Beyond Cross-Modal Reconstruction: Participant-Level Evaluation of sEMG-Kinematic Coupling in Post-Stroke Gait
papers.abstract: Accurate cross-modal reconstruction is often treated as evidence of physiological coupling, although it may simply reflect temporal patterns shared across participants. We tested whether frozen bidirectional models captured subject-specific neuromuscular coupling between electromyographic activity and gait kinematics in 82 held-out able-bodied and 43 post-stroke participants. Complete source-modality removal and cross-participant source substitution, along with a cycle-position-age-sex template baseline, were applied. Learned bilateral asymmetry was also compared with transparent waveform and derivative asymmetry for predicting Performance-Oriented Mobility Assessment (POMA) scores in the case of repeated nested cross-validation. Complete source removal increased reconstruction RMSE by 6.90% for electromyography-to-kinematics and 11.38% in the reverse direction. In contrast, cross-participant substitution increased RMSE by only 1.68% and 1.67%, respectively, while the template reduced RMSE by 2.89% and 0.55%. For POMA prediction, walking speed, age, and sex achieved an MAE of 3.693, compared with 4.229 and 4.427 after adding absolute and signed learned asymmetry, respectively. In all of the 20 repeated evaluations, all asymmetry representations performed worse than the covariate baseline.
